description: Umbrella orchestrator. Create one Installer Composition per Krateo platform installation. It registers and emits the component blueprints in dependency order. Pinned to installer 2.7.0.

authn.description: Umbrella-owned settings for the RSA key authn signs JWTs with. The Secret itself is created by this chart before authn starts; authn mounts it and publishes the matching public key at GET /.well-known/jwks.json.

keyGeneration.description: Which generation of the signing key to serve. 1 renders authn's own chart defaults (Secret authn-jwt-signing-key, kid krateo-authn-key-1), so existing clusters see no diff and no upgrade rotates the key. Raising it to N creates Secret authn-jwt-signing-key-N with a fresh RSA key and makes authn mount it and advertise kid krateo-authn-key-N. Because authn has no per-token revocation, a bump is the only way to stop honouring already-issued tokens -- it signs out every session, and nothing lowers it back automatically. The previous Secret is left in the cluster; removing key material is a separate, deliberate act.
keyGeneration.title: JWT signing key generation

overlapGenerations.description: How many RETIRED generations keep VERIFYING after a keyGeneration bump. 0 (the default when absent) is today's behaviour exactly: a bump signs out every session, which is what keyGeneration is for. N > 0 derives previousKeys entries for generations keyGeneration-1 .. keyGeneration-N and FORCES them onto the component, so a rotation stops SIGNING with the old key while still honouring tokens it already issued. Carries NO default on purpose -- crdgen materialises installer-schema defaults into every install's CR, where they beat the chart's own values.yaml, so a default would pin this against any future chart change. A previous key NEVER signs: authn keeps only its public half, so retaining the retired private key for the overlap is a security cost rather than a necessity. HOW LONG TO HOLD IT: an entry can go once every token it signed has expired, at most AUTHN_KUBECONFIG_CRT_EXPIRES_IN (24h by default), which also clamps the login JWT; delegated tokens are at most 15m. So 1, held at least 24h after a bump, covers every live token. ORDERING THAT MATTERS: lower this (dropping a generation from the list) BEFORE deleting that generation's Secret, never in the same apply -- authn refuses to START on a listed Secret that is absent and the pod hangs mounting the volume. A keyGeneration JUMP (1 -> 3) never created the skipped generation's Secret, so the derivation measures existence and omits what was never written; nothing is lost, because no token was ever signed by a key that never existed.
overlapGenerations.title: JWT verification overlap (retired generations still honoured)

bootstrap.description: When true, install core-provider as a conditional subchart dependency (gated by bootstrap.coreProvider.enabled) so a bare-cluster helm install self-bootstraps. The hook-weighting that orders bootstrap is on the installer's own self-bootstrap Job, not the subchart.

waitForSynced.description: When true, the bootstrap adds a final hook wave that blocks until the Installer CR is Synced (honest `deployed`), at the cost of a longer client-interruption window. Off by default.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap (composition engine)

componentValues.description: Per-component Composition spec overrides, STRICTLY TYPED against each pinned component's chart schema. This is a HAND-CURATED, deliberate override surface: every leaf is explicitly typed and unknown keys are REJECTED (additionalProperties is false on every object). No free-form escapes remain anywhere in this schema (neither an open additionalProperties nor the k8s preserve-unknown extension) — enforced in CI by .github/workflows/check-no-unknowns.yaml. Invariants: each component's `global` is the fixed engine-injected block (plumbing InjectGlobalValues) plus imageRegistry; `resources` is k8s ResourceRequirements (limits/requests each with cpu/memory); label, annotation and nodeSelector maps are typed string maps. To expose a NEW override knob for a component, add it here explicitly and typed — do not reintroduce a free-form object. Deep-merged into the rendered Composition spec; the installer-computed wiring (service.type/config/vertexAI/hitlApproval) stays authoritative and wins on any leaf conflict.

access-review.description: Full-coverage override surface for the access-review chart (pinned 0.1.8). Every key of the chart's values.yaml is typed and nothing is left open: componentValues is additionalProperties:false and check-no-unknowns.py fails any PR reintroducing additionalProperties:true or x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields. `resources`, `podSecurityContext` and `securityContext` are type:object with NO additionalProperties in the chart's own schema -- neither false nor true, so permissive -- and acmp confirmed the chart does not mean to accept arbitrary fields, so they are closed here to exactly the keys its values.yaml sets.

extraEnv.description: Kubernetes EnvVar entries for the access-review controller, mirrored verbatim from the chart's own values.schema.json so the two cannot drift. Closed at every level: the chart REFUSES POD_NAMESPACE and POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT. To get audit records out, AUDIT-4 needs OTEL_ENABLED=true and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set to the collector base URL here; the component appends the logs path itself. No default: a default in this file would propagate into the Installer CR and become a silent live override.

global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.
global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

rbac.description: Roles the controller may bind, scoped by resourceNames. The chart's own schema forbids a wildcard and an empty name; those constraints are MIRRORED here so a componentValues override cannot widen what the chart itself refuses.

agentgateway.description: Spec for the agentgateway edge component (feature: ingress), deep-merged into its Composition. Mirrors oci://ghcr.io/krateo-blueprints/charts/agentgateway; renders the platform GatewayClass + Gateway over the bundled upstream controller. gateway.name defaults to krateo-gateway and MUST equal exposure.gatewayRef.name and cert-manager-issuers' acme.gatewayRef.name; leave unset to accept the aligned defaults.

resources.description:
Resources is the resource requirements for the server container.
Applied as a whole: operator defaults are used only when all resource fields are empty.

claims.description:
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims,
that are used by this container.

This field depends on the
DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers.

items.description: ResourceClaim references one entry in PodSpec.ResourceClaims.

name.description:
Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of
the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available
inside a container.

request.description:
Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim.
If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise
only the result of this request.

limits.description:
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

requests.description:
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified,
otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

gateway.description: The chart marks `gateway` root-required with `name` and `listeners` required inside it. The default is on THIS object, not only on its children: structural-schema defaulting fills fields of objects that are PRESENT, so child defaults never apply when the parent is absent and the CR is rejected for the missing required key. Values copied from the chart's own values.yaml — the chart defaulting them does NOT satisfy the generated CRD, because crdgen keeps `required` and the CR's spec is built from componentValues (installer#489).

agentgateway-policies.description: JWT authentication and three-layer RBAC for the Krateo kagent fleet, rendered as agentgateway Gateway/HTTPRoute/AgentgatewayPolicy/AgentgatewayBackend objects. Values double as the Composition spec (a partial override merged over the chart defaults), so no property is schema-required; array items still require their own keys.

enabled.description: Render the Gateway-level Allow policy carrying layers 1 and 3. false leaves the gateway authenticating without authorizing.

budgets.description: LLM TOKEN budgets on the LLM route. On a route whose backend declares an AI provider, traffic.rateLimit.local[].tokens counts LLM tokens rather than requests, so this is a spend cap. FOUR AGENTGATEWAY BEHAVIOURS TO SIZE AGAINST: usage is post-hoc so the request that busts the budget COMPLETES and the next gets 429; rate limiting runs BEFORE the prompt guards so a guard-rejected request has already spent its tokens; ONE HOUR is the longest window local rate limiting can express; and buckets are PER PROXY REPLICA, so gateway.parameters.hpa multiplies every number here. Cached input counts too.

enabled.description: Off by default: a budget that is too small takes the whole fleet mute, since every agent's model call crosses this route, and there is no fleet-wide number that is right by default.

gateway.description: The fleet-wide ceiling: ONE bucket shared by every caller on the LLM route.

burst.description: Extra allowance above the steady rate. 0 = none.

inheritance.description: Override = no route-level rate-limit policy may relax this ceiling. Default so an install carrying its own route policy is not surprised on upgrade.

requests.description: A second, independent cap on request COUNT - a backstop against a runaway agent loop making thousands of cheap calls. 0 = no request cap.

tokens.description: LLM tokens per unit across everyone. 0 = no token cap.

unit.description: Hours is the longest window local rate limiting can express.

tiers.description: Tiered budgets, each entry its OWN independent bucket, FIRST MATCH WINS. A users entry is a genuine per-that-user budget; a groups entry is ONE bucket the whole group shares. Max 16 entries, at most ONE entry with no subjects and it must be LAST (the unconditional fallback). A per-user budget exists only for users NAMED HERE - there is no automatic bucket-per-caller with local rate limiting.

certReplayHop.description: Cert-replay hop (issue #12): a per-user-RBAC hop so kagent tool calls run under the CALLING USER's RBAC (kagent-tools with tokenPassthrough, mounting the hop's kubeconfig). This is the policies chart's ONLY Layer 5 mechanism (the earlier SAR-on-claims decider, nativeRbac, was removed) and is default-on. The installer auto-wires image.pullSecrets from registryAuth for the private cert-replay-hop image (a third private-krateo-agentiko-image component, alongside repo-mcp-server and chart-gate); the rest are the policies chart's own knobs.

audience.description: Expected JWT audience (empty = accept the chart default).

enabled.description: Render the hop + route kagent tool calls through it. Default true.

pullSecrets.description: IMAGE-pull secrets for the private hop image. Auto-wired by the installer from registryAuth (the derived krateo-registry-image-pull dockerconfigjson); set explicitly to override, or [] to opt out.

issuer.description: Expected JWT issuer the hop validates. Default krateo.io.

targetRoute.description: The kagent-tools route the hop fronts. Default kagent-tools.

cors.description: CORS for the gateway. Only needed when a BROWSER calls it directly (the Krateo portal's Autopilot rail does): the browser sends an unauthenticated OPTIONS preflight first, which the authorization policy would 403, and refuses the real request unless the answer carries Access-Control-Allow-*. Short-circuits the preflight ONLY — a real request with no/bad token is still 403/401. Server-to-server callers are unaffected. The Krateo installer enables it with features.agentGateway.

allowCredentials.description: Leave false: no cookies are involved, and true alongside allowOrigins ['*'] is rejected by browsers.

allowOrigins.description: Origins allowed to call the gateway from a browser. Defaults to '*' because the portal's browser-facing origin is not knowable in-cluster; pin it to the real portal origin when you know it. Safe by default only while allowCredentials is false — the credential is a Bearer header the page must set itself, not a cookie.

maxAge.description: Seconds a browser may cache the preflight answer.

costCatalog.description: Model cost catalog. agentgateway meters tokens on its own but prices nothing without one: llm.cost.* stays unset and agentgateway_gen_ai_client_cost_usd_total stays 0, and the pinned proxy ships no built-in catalog. The pricing data is a vendored artefact in the chart, rendered into a ConfigMap and named from gateway.parameters. THE CATALOG IS KEYED BY GATEWAY PROVIDER ID AND THE ID FOLLOWS THE ENDPOINT, NOT THE MODEL VENDOR: gemini by API key is gcp.gemini, the same model via Vertex is gcp.vertex_ai, and Claude served by Vertex prices under gcp.vertex_ai rather than anthropic.

enabled.description: false = no ConfigMap and no modelCatalog source. Token metering and budgets are unaffected; only the dollar figures disappear.

key.description: Data key inside the ConfigMap. agentgateway defaults to catalog.json.

overrides.description: Rates merged over the vendored catalog, in the same {<provider id>: {models: {<model id>: {rates: {...}}}}} shape - for a model the vendored file does not price yet. Rates are USD per 1M tokens AS STRINGS: the parser reads them as decimals and rejects JSON numbers.

providers.description: Provider blocks to keep from the vendored catalog, by gateway provider id. A PROVIDER THAT IS ABSENT PRICES AT 0 SILENTLY - a model missing the catalog is not an error, and the only signal is agentgateway_cost_catalog_lookups_total broken down by its status label. A render guard checks the provider in use is listed.

endpointRules.description: Layer 1 — which subjects may reach which agent's A2A endpoint directly.

agents.description: Agent names, or ["*"] for the whole /api/a2a/<ns>/ prefix.

subjects.description: Who a rule grants access to. The matchers are OR'd; at least one must be set, otherwise the rule would deny everyone. `anyAuthenticated` is IGNORED when `users` or `groups` is set: these blocks are deep-merged maps, so a caller narrowing a rule to a group never sees the default `anyAuthenticated: true` disappear, and OR'ing it back in would silently restore access to everyone. Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

anyAuthenticated.description: Any request carrying a token this gateway validated. Ignored when `users` or `groups` is set.

groups.description: Values that must appear in the groups claim (authn: `groups`, a list of strings).

users.description: Values of the user claim (authn: the username in `sub`).

extraAllowExpressions.description: Extra CEL expressions appended verbatim to the Gateway Allow policy. OR'd with the generated ones, so they can only widen access.

extraMcpServers.description: Additive: appended to the agentgateway-policies chart's mcpServers (extraMcpServers knob, chart>=0.1.17). In-cluster MCP servers to front. Each entry renders an AgentgatewayBackend + route (required once the kagent controller proxies agent egress) and its per-tool rules. External MCP servers are not proxied and must not be listed.

name.description: Service name, which is also the x-kagent-host value (<service>.<namespace>).

path.description: MCP endpoint path on the server. Default /mcp.

toolRules.description: Layer 2 — each entry restricts the named tools to the given subjects. Rules are AND'd into one expression, so a rule can only narrow access. Tools named nowhere stay open.

Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

Each entry renders the header-matched route, the token passthrough, the anonymous agent-card allowance and the delegation rule.

fullnameOverride.description: Override the full object name prefix.

allowedRoutesFrom.description: Which namespaces may attach routes to this Gateway.

create.description: Render the Gateway. false = attach to a Gateway someone else owns.

gcpServiceAccount.description: The GCP service account that both gateway KSAs should impersonate via Workload Identity, as a full email. Setting it adds the iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account annotation to the krateo-agent-gateway and krateo-agent-gateway-platform KSAs plus a parametersRef on the platform Gateway. INERT until the cluster's node pool runs GKE_METADATA, so it is safe to set before the node-pool switch and pointless before the IAM binding exists. Unset, the chart renders byte-identical to the behaviour without it. Declared because this gateway node is a closed object: an undeclared key here is pruned silently with every CI check green.

internalDataPlane.description: Close the agent data-plane listener (port) to the internet using the standard two-Gateway split: flip THIS (agent) Gateway's controller-provisioned proxy Service to ClusterIP (all its listeners in-cluster only, Service name/DNS unchanged) via an AgentgatewayParameters, and move the platform listeners to a SECOND, real Gateway (platformGatewayName) whose own controller-provisioned Service keeps the controller's default LoadBalancer type. Requires platformRoutes. Off => byte-identical.

listenerName.description: Listener name; every route attaches to it by sectionName.

mcpBackendHash.description: MCP-backend roll-guard. The installer forcePaths a hash of every MCP-server component's <name>:<version> here (compositions.yaml); the chart stamps it on the proxy pod template so the proxy pod rolls whenever an MCP-server version changes. Installer-managed — do not set by hand.

name.description: Gateway name; also the name of the proxy Service the controller provisions, i.e. the host in the kagent controller's proxy.url.

parameters.description: The proxy Deployment the agentgateway controller provisions from this Gateway, rendered as an AgentgatewayParameters the Gateway names in infrastructure.parametersRef. That placement is what makes the model cost catalog work at all: a GatewayClass-level AgentgatewayParameters resolves ConfigMap references from the wrong namespace. Ignored when gateway.create is false.

deployment.description: Strategic-merge overlay on the proxy Deployment spec the controller generates, applied after every typed field. The escape hatch for anything this block does not model.

enabled.description: false = none of the typed fields below and no cost catalog: the proxy takes the controller chart's defaults, llm.cost is unset and every request prices at 0. It does not always remove the object — internalDataPlane and mcpBackendHash ride the same AgentgatewayParameters (a parametersRef holds one name), so with either on it still renders with only their fields.

env.description: Appended verbatim to the proxy container's env; the controller merges these over its own.

hpa.description: HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the proxy. Safe for throughput and NOT safe for local budgets: a local rate-limit bucket lives in the proxy PROCESS, so N replicas enforce N times every budget. A render guard rejects enabling this alongside budgets.

logging.description: Proxy logging. Empty level = the controller's default (info).

level.description: RUST_LOG syntax, e.g. info or a comma-separated per-module setting.

pdb.description: PodDisruptionBudget for the proxy. minAvailable:1 with a single replica forbids voluntary eviction of the only pod, which is right for a fleet-wide chokepoint and WILL stall a node drain.

resources.description: Proxy container resources. Every A2A, MCP and LLM call in the fleet crosses this one pod.

service.description: Strategic-merge overlay on the proxy Service spec.

platformGatewayName.description: Name of the second Gateway that carries the platform listeners (and gets the platform LoadBalancer) when internalDataPlane is on. Empty => derived as `<gateway.name>-platform`.

platformHostname.description: #115: DNS hostname for the platform LoadBalancer. When set (installer passes exposure.tls.host), the platform Gateway's Service is annotated external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname, so a deployed external-dns publishes/updates a DNS record following the LB IP (DNS-follows-LB). Only meaningful in the two-gateway split (internalDataPlane). Empty => no annotation, byte-identical.

gatewayClass.description: The GatewayClass the Gateway below names. The controller that reconciles it is a separate release (chart agentgateway-controller).

controllerName.description: Must equal the agentgateway controller's own name, or the class is never reconciled.

create.description: Render the GatewayClass. false = one of this name already exists; it is cluster-scoped, so only one release may own it.

guardrails.description: Content guardrails on the LLM traffic: PII and secret masking, company-data redaction, prompt-injection blocking, and the external moderation services. An agentgateway prompt guard is a `backend.ai` policy and only runs on a route whose backend declares `spec.ai.provider` — that route is the top-level `llm` block; these policies attach to it. Disabling this removes every guard and leaves the route in place, so the traffic keeps flowing through the gateway, just unguarded.

bedrockGuardrails.description: Layer 2 — AWS Bedrock Guardrails, usable in front of any provider (not only a Bedrock model). The one external layer that also honours `scope`, so it can inspect tool arguments and tool results as well as the prompt.

apply.description: Which directions this layer runs in. Each direction is a separate guard entry and counts against the 8-per-direction ceiling.

response.description: Inspect the model's answer on its way back.

region.description: SigV4 signing region, when the target service is not in the gateway's region.

key.description: Inline key. Least secure.

extraResponseGuards.description: Guard entries appended verbatim to `promptGuard.response`. Same caveat.

regex.description: Layer 1 — deterministic, sub-millisecond, no external dependency. Each class renders at most two guard entries (one per direction), evaluated in the order listed here.

combine.description: agentgateway allows at most 8 guards per direction, and the full set here (7 default regex classes + moderation + Model Armor + Bedrock + webhook) is 11. WhenNeeded (the default) keeps one entry per class while the total fits and folds every same-action, same-scope class into one entry once it would exceed 8. Never always keeps them separate and fails the render with an actionable message instead. Always folds unconditionally — cheapest on slots, and the rejection message stops naming which class fired.

streaming.description: Run the guards on STREAMED responses too. Disabled upstream by default to protect streaming throughput; Enabled here because kagent streams and response guards would otherwise never run. Note the asymmetry: a streamed response can be REJECTED but not MASKED — matched content is already in flight, so a Mask response guard passes it through unmodified and records nothing. Request guards are unaffected (a request is always buffered).

targetRefs.description: What the guardrail policy attaches to. Empty = the route the top-level `llm` block renders, which is the only route on this Gateway carrying LLM traffic. Set it to attach the same guards to an HTTPRoute or AgentgatewayBackend someone else owns (and then usually `llm.enabled: false`). The API group is filled in from the kind.

sectionName.description: A named LLM provider inside a multi-provider AgentgatewayBackend.

webhook.description: Layer 3 — your own guardrail server. This chart ships none on purpose: the point of the layer is that the logic is yours (a DLP tool you already run, an NER model, a compliance service). Deploy a server that speaks the Guardrail Webhook API — POST /request and POST /response, answering pass, mask or reject — and name it here.

apply.description: Which directions this layer runs in. Each direction is a separate guard entry and counts against the 8-per-direction ceiling.

request.description: Inspect the prompt on its way to the provider.

response.description: Inspect the model's answer on its way back.

backendRef.description: The webhook server. A Service, or an agentgateway.dev/AgentgatewayBackend for anything off-cluster.

namespace.description: Empty = this release's namespace. A different one also needs a ReferenceGrant.

failureMode.description: What happens when your server is down or errors. FailClosed (the default) is the safe choice and the expensive one: your webhook becomes a hard dependency of every LLM turn. FailOpen lets the exchange through unguarded.

forwardHeaderMatches.description: Which of the client's own headers to forward. None by default. Gateway API HTTPHeaderMatch entries, passed through verbatim.

headers.description: CEL-computed headers on the outgoing webhook call, evaluated against the ORIGINAL client request — so `jwt.sub` carries the caller's identity through to your server. The `:path` pseudo-header overrides the default /request and /response paths, and its value is a CEL expression, so a literal path needs inner quotes: '"/api/guardrails/request"'.

request.description: What the client is told when this guard rejects. Both empty = the gateway's own default text and 403.

message.description: Response body returned instead of the model's answer.

response.description: What the client is told when this guard rejects. Both empty = the gateway's own default text and 403.

message.description: Response body returned instead of the model's answer.

audiences.description: Allowed aud values. MUST stay empty for authn, which emits no aud claim.

enabled.description: Render the JWT authentication policy and the token-passthrough policy.

groupsClaim.description: Claim carrying the group list (authn: groups).

issuer.description: Must equal the token's iss claim (authn: krateo.io).

cacheDuration.description: How long a fetched JWKS is reused. agentgateway rejects anything below 5m.

namespace.description: Its namespace. Empty = release namespace; anything else also renders a ReferenceGrant.

mode.description: Strict = no token is a 401, and each sub-agent route gets its own route-scoped Optional policy so the tokenless agent-card fetch still lands. Optional = one Gateway-wide policy; anonymous traffic is denied by authorization with a 403. Permissive never rejects and should not be used.

userClaim.description: Claim carrying the user identity (authn: sub).

agentNamespace.description: Namespace of the Agent CRs — the <namespace> segment of /api/a2a/<namespace>/<agent>/. Empty = release namespace.

service.description: kagent controller Service; it serves every agent's A2A endpoint.

llm.description: The LLM hop: the AI backend the agents' model calls resolve to, and the OpenAI-compatible route they arrive on. INFRASTRUCTURE rather than a guardrail detail — once the calls arrive here every `backend.ai` policy agentgateway has becomes available on them, and guardrails are only the first consumer (rate limits and token budgets, cost controls, model aliases, failover across providers, prompt enrichment and per-model RBAC all attach to this same route). Disabling it hands the hop back: the route disappears and the agents go straight to the provider.

anthropic.description: Anthropic. Both fields as for gemini.

auth.description: An API-key credential. Set `secretRef` (preferred) or `key`; `secretRef` wins if both are given.

key.description: Inline key. Least secure — it lands in the Composition spec and in helm's release Secret in cleartext.

location.description: Where the credential is written on the outgoing request. Empty = the `Authorization` header with a `Bearer ` prefix. Exactly one of the three when set.

secretRef.description: A Kubernetes Secret holding one credential. Empty `name` = the credential source is unset.

key.description: Data key to read. Empty = the location's default (`Authorization` for a header credential, `credentials.json` for GCP). A `Bearer ` prefix is stripped only from the default `Authorization` key, so a raw key must name its own data key.

name.description: Secret name, in this release's namespace.

model.description: Model override. Empty = from the request.

bedrock.description: AWS Bedrock as the model provider (distinct from `bedrockGuardrails`, which is a guardrail service and can front any provider).

auth.description: AWS credentials for SigV4 signing. An empty `secretRef.name` means the default AWS credential chain (IRSA, instance profile, environment).

assumeRole.description: STS AssumeRole settings, passed through verbatim. Mutually exclusive with secretRef.

region.description: SigV4 signing region, when the target service is not in the gateway's region.

name.description: Secret with `accessKey`, `secretKey` and optionally `sessionToken`.

serviceName.description: SigV4 service name. Typed AWS backends supply this themselves.

model.description: Model override. Empty = from the request.

benchRoute.description: Guardrail-EXEMPT second HTTPRoute onto the SAME AI backend (same provider/credential), for benchmark measurement ONLY — OFF by default; keep it off in production. The fleet guardrails MASK identifiers in flight (e.g. checkout-db.otel-demo.internal -> checkout-db.<masked>), which is right for the fleet and fatal for an RCA benchmark scored on whether the answer NAMES the failing entity; the guard policy targets the LLM route by name, so this differently-named route is outside it and the fleet keeps every guard while the benchmark runs. While on, the cluster has an unmasked, credentialed path to the provider, so its identity rules are the narrowest in this chart: route-scoped jwtAuthentication:Strict (a tokenless call is 401 even where the gateway JWT mode is Optional) and an authorization Require rule that REFUSES anyAuthenticated — subjects.users/groups must name someone or the render fails. It also fails render unless llm.enabled, authorization.enabled and jwt.enabled are all true and routePrefix is a non-nested, '/'-prefixed path. Mirrors agentgateway-policies llm.benchRoute (PR#27).

enabled.description: false (default) renders not one bench object. Set true, for a named window, only on the cluster you are benchmarking — and only together with subjects, or the render fails.

routePrefix.description: The bench route's path prefix and the harness base URL. Must start with '/' and MUST NOT nest with llm.routePrefix (a nested prefix would be authorized by the LLM route's anyAuthenticated clause instead of the named subjects). Keep the '/v1' ending so <routePrefix>/chat/completions is detected as OpenAI-style. Default /bench/v1.

subjects.description: WHO MAY USE IT. The one matcher in this chart that REFUSES anyAuthenticated: name users or groups, or the render fails. Both empty by default so enabling the route on its own fails rather than rendering a route on a matcher nobody chose.

groups.description: Named group subjects allowed on the bench route (only as narrow as the group's membership).

users.description: Named user subjects (matched on the validated jwt claim) allowed on the bench route.

callerAuth.description: Who may use the LLM route — the traffic-layer gate for this hop, the analogue of `mcpTraffic` for the MCP hop. It matters more than it looks: the gateway is browser-reachable in the Krateo portal's exposure model, so an ungated LLM route is an open, credentialed proxy to your provider account.

mode.description: Strict = no key or a bad key is 401. Optional and Permissive exist for migrations; both let keyless requests reach the authorization layer.

mode.description: Jwt — kagent's `apiKeyPassthrough` forwards the CALLER's authn token as the LLM credential, the Gateway JWT policy validates it, and `subjects` decides who may spend tokens; a turn with no caller token (an unauthenticated webhook trigger, a cron) has nothing to forward and is denied. ApiKey — a shared key from a Secret, validated on the route; pick this for callers that are not user-driven. Anonymous — path-only allow, safe ONLY when this Gateway is unreachable from outside the cluster.

subjects.description: Jwt mode: who may spend provider tokens. Same matcher shape as every other rule in this chart.

health.description: Passive health checking on the AI backend. WITHOUT THIS NOTHING IS EVER EVICTED AND FAILOVER NEVER HAPPENS, however many llm.tiers are configured - which is why it defaults on even though tiers do not: with one provider it is a no-op and it is already correct the day a second tier is added.

consecutiveFailures.description: Failures in a row before eviction. 0 = score-based eviction only.

duration.description: BASE eviction duration; repeated evictions of the same provider back off multiplicatively.

unhealthyCondition.description: CEL over the response. 429 MUST be listed explicitly or a THROTTLED provider is never evicted - and agentgateway uses that response's Retry-After as the eviction duration when present, so listing it is also what honours the provider's own backoff. Connection-level failures count as unhealthy regardless.

limits.description: Abuse bounds on the fleet LLM route (agentgateway-policies llm.limits): rate limit (requests + tokens/min), request body cap, per-request timeout. The chart defaults these ON; override here only to tune per install (e.g. raise tokensPerMinute on a bench cluster).

routePrefix.description: Path prefix of the rendered route, and therefore the `openAI.baseUrl` every agent gets: http://<gateway.name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:<gateway.port><routePrefix>. Deliberately not a bare `/v1`: this Gateway also carries /api/a2a/…, /mcp and the header-matched `/` sub-agent routes. kagent appends `/chat/completions`, so the full path still ends in `/v1/chat/completions` and agentgateway's route-type detection matches it.

tiers.description: Ordered failover tiers. Empty = one upstream from llm.provider and no failover (spec.ai.provider). Non-empty = spec.ai.groups[], one group per entry in order: the first tier is preferred and traffic falls to the next only when every provider in the current tier has been EVICTED by llm.health. Max 8. A TIER MUST PIN ITS OWN MODEL - agents ask for the id in their ModelConfig and that id does not exist on another vendor's API, so an unpinned fallback 404s on arrival. Each tier reuses the per-provider auth above, so tiers need one credential Secret per provider used. Load balancing within a tier is automatic and needs no configuration.

model.description: Model id on THAT provider. Required - see the block description.

provider.description: Which provider serves this tier. `custom` is single-upstream only and cannot be a tier.

toolHistory.description: How much of the tool-result history an agent loop re-sends is kept. Every step of a loop resends every earlier tool result verbatim, so prefill grows quadratically in tool calls.

truncate.description: Truncate tool results the model has already acted on, and bound the newest one. Rendered as a stage of the backend's composed `messages` rewrite, applied before provider conversion, so it is provider-independent and invisible to the agent. Needs agentgateway-policies >= 0.2.10.

enabled.description: On by default in agentgateway-policies >= 0.2.10. It is lossy: a fact the model needs from an older tool result becomes unreadable mid-turn and nothing fetches it back. Set false for an agent fleet that reads back across long evidence chains.

maxChars.description: Characters kept from each already-acted-on tool result; the newest is bounded by newestMaxChars instead. Defaults to 8000, which leaves six results in seven whole while still removing ~70% of tool-output characters. Lower it if prefill still dominates; raise it for agents that read back.

newestMaxChars.description: Characters kept from the newest tool result, half from its head and half from its tail; 0 keeps it whole at any length. Must be 0 or at least maxChars. Defaults to 100000 (~25-30k tokens). Needs agentgateway-policies >= 0.2.31.

agentMaxChars.description: Characters kept from an older tool result that answers a call to another agent (a kagent agent tool, named <namespace>__NS__<agent>), half from its head and half from its tail; 0 keeps it whole. Must be 0 or at least maxChars. Such a result is the agent's report and costs minutes to produce again; cut to maxChars, the caller re-runs the agent.

transformations.description: Raw CEL rewrites of the LLM request body, for a rewrite no chart feature covers. Each entry replaces one top-level field of the OpenAI-shaped request with its expression's result; the body is readable as `llmRequest`. An entry for the messages field fails the component's render when a chart fragment already composes it. Needs agentgateway-policies >= 0.2.10.

expression.description: CEL expression evaluated against the request body, readable as `llmRequest`.

field.description: Top-level request-body field the expression's result replaces, e.g. `messages`.

vertexai.description: Vertex AI path. Leave `auth.gcp.secretRef` empty to use ambient credentials; off GKE, point it at a service-account key JSON (installer: vertexAI.secretName/secretKey).

auth.description: Google Cloud credentials. All fields empty = ambient discovery (on GKE, the proxy pod's node SA — the same path the agents use for Vertex today).

projectId.description: GCP project hosting Vertex AI. Required for this provider.

region.description: `global` routes across regions instead of pinning one Dynamic Shared Quota pool; `us`/`eu` are restricted multi-region endpoints; anything else is a regional location.

loadShedding.description: Hard caps on how much work the proxy holds at once. Past a cap it REJECTS immediately instead of queueing, so a runaway agent loop cannot take the proxy - and with it every A2A, MCP and LLM call in the fleet - down by exhausting it. A room-capacity limit, not a rate limit: budgets says 'you have had enough', this says 'the proxy is full'. Shed traffic lands in agentgateway_requests_shed_total and agentgateway_downstream_connections_shed_total. REQUIRES THE v1.5.0 agentgateway CRDs for the two counts - frontend.http.maxConcurrentRequests and frontend.tcp.maxConnections do not exist in v1.4.1 and the API server rejects the policy there. maxConnectionDuration works on either.

enabled.description: Off by default: a cap chosen without load data is as likely to shed real traffic as to protect anything, and the numbers have to be picked against gateway.parameters.resources - a cap far above what the memory limit can serve is a slower way to OOM, not protection.

maxConcurrentRequests.description: Concurrent in-flight requests. 0 = unlimited. Needs v1.5.0 CRDs.

maxConnectionDuration.description: Force a connection closed after this long however busy it is, so a long-lived client rebalances onto a new proxy replica instead of pinning to one. Empty = never. Works on the v1.4.1 CRDs.

maxConnections.description: Active downstream connections on the listener; over the limit they are closed immediately. 0 = unlimited. Higher than maxConcurrentRequests because kagent holds keepalive connections open between turns. Needs v1.5.0 CRDs.

mcpEntry.description: The MCP entry point for IDEs: /mcp on the portal's TLS listener -> the kagent controller's built-in MCP server. Admits exactly the subjects of the endpointRules entries that grant agents ["*"]. The chart renders it only when a platformRoutes listener carries tls. The chart's OWN default is enabled: true, so this node is the only lever that can keep /mcp closed; it deliberately carries no schema default, so leaving the key unset leaves the chart default in force.

toolRules.description: Layer 2 — each entry restricts the named tools to the given subjects. Rules are AND'd into one expression, so a rule can only narrow access. Tools named nowhere stay open.

subjects.description: Who a rule grants access to. The matchers are OR'd; at least one must be set, otherwise the rule would deny everyone. `anyAuthenticated` is IGNORED when `users` or `groups` is set: these blocks are deep-merged maps, so a caller narrowing a rule to a group never sees the default `anyAuthenticated: true` disappear, and OR'ing it back in would silently restore access to everyone. Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

observability.description: Three signals with three different costs, hence three switches: metrics are free Prometheus labels on the proxy's own :15020, accessLog is one OTLP row per request in ClickHouse (the chargeback record), and tracing (a sibling top-level key) is the expensive one. Every reading of these numbers carries agentgateway's own caveats: a 429 is post-hoc so a budget row can exceed its limit, rate limiting runs before the prompt guards so guard-rejected requests still appear as spend, and cached input counts toward both tokens and cost.

accessLog.description: One OTLP row per request: who called, which agent served it, which tool ran, which model answered, how many tokens, how many dollars, how much budget is left and which guard intervened. THE ROWS ARRIVE AS LogAttributes MAP ENTRIES WITH AN EMPTY Body - agentgateway builds each LogRecord out of attributes and never sets a body - so SQL over default.otel_logs must read LogAttributes['...'] (a String, so cast it) and never Body. ServiceName is the GATEWAY's name.

attributes.description: Extra entries as name -> CEL expression. Guard every claim read with has(): an unauthenticated request has no jwt object at all and an unguarded expression throws.

auditFacts.description: Whether the access-log policy emits the six AUDIT-4 fact attributes: principal, act, backend_host, baggage_session, source_xff and user_agent. The chart DEFAULTS IT TO TRUE, so the facts arrive without setting anything -- this key exists so a cluster can turn them OFF, which is otherwise impossible because this accessLog node is a closed object and an undeclared key is pruned silently with every CI check green. Declared with NO default here, so the component's own default governs unless a cluster opts out explicitly. Note what the six are: `principal` is an identity class derived from the JWT (jwt.act.principal on a delegated RFC 8693 token, else jwt.principal), while baggage_session, source_xff and user_agent are CLIENT-CONTROLLED correlation keys and must not be treated as identity. agentgateway-policies 0.2.27 filters any baggage session value starting with `eyJ` so a JWT cannot be logged as a session id, and no token appears in any of the six expressions.

enabled.description: false = no access log policy. The three RBAC layers still ENFORCE; they just leave no record, and observability.alerts has nothing to count.

filter.description: CEL gate on whether a row is emitted at all. Empty = every request, which is the point of an audit record.

guardrails.description: WHICH GUARD FIRED. guardrails[] carries one entry per INTERVENTION with the guard kind, phase, action and reason; content-bearing fields are never included, so it is safe to store. A CLEAN PASS EMITS NOTHING - the attribute is absent, not empty - so it complements agentgateway_guardrail_checks_total rather than replacing it.

includeUser.description: On here, unlike metrics and tracing, because a log row is one row per request rather than a permanent series - so per-user attribution is cheap in exactly this one place.

otlp.description: Where the rows go. MUST be a collector whose `logs` pipeline declares an otlp receiver. On a stock Krateo install that is the ClickStack DAEMONSET collector, whose stock logs pipeline is receivers:[filelog] only - so the clickstack-chart change adding otlp there is a PREREQUISITE. Without it the rows reach a port with no consumer and are dropped with no error at either end.

promptLogging.description: Prompt and completion TEXT. Its own switch, off, and it should stay off unless someone has decided the retention question: turning it on writes every prompt a user types, and every answer the model returns, into ClickHouse - where the otel_logs TTL, not this chart, decides how long it lives.

removeAttributes.description: Default attribute names to drop from the row.

toolCalls.description: Which tools the model asked for. REFERENCING llm.toolCalls IS WHAT TURNS EXTRACTION ON - it is not collected otherwise - and it has a documented cost on large responses.

includeArguments.description: Tool ARGUMENTS are user content, so this is the same privacy question as promptLogging. UNSET follows promptLogging.enabled; set it explicitly to decouple them.

alerts.description: Budget breaches as INCIDENTS. An Alert CR (observability.krateo.io) is reconciled into a HyperDX alert; while it fires, alert-provider opens an Incident with an incident-agent RCA, which the portal shows under /incidents. These count the accessLog rows, so they need accessLog.enabled AND the Alert CRD (alert-provider-crd, features.specialistAgents). spec.where edits DO NOT PROPAGATE to the live HyperDX alert - change one by deleting and recreating the CR.

enabled.description: false = no Alert CRs. Budgets still return 429 and access logs still record it; there is simply no incident raised.

exhausted.description: Fires when the LLM route starts returning 429 - a budget is exhausted and turns are already failing. An incident, not a warning.

nearlyExhausted.description: The WARNING, and the whole reason budget_remaining is an access-log attribute: x-ratelimit-remaining rides ALLOWED responses too, so the tail of a budget is visible before the first 429.

remainingBelow.description: Absolute token allowance, not a fraction: local buckets are per-replica and per-tier, so there is no single 'the limit' to take a percentage of. Roughly a tenth of the smallest budget.

metrics.description: Custom metric fields are flattened into EVERY metric label set, the gen_ai ones included, so this one policy turns agentgateway_gen_ai_client_token_usage and agentgateway_gen_ai_client_cost_usd_total into per-team series. NOTHING IN A STOCK KRATEO INSTALL SCRAPES THIS: agentgateway exports metrics by Prometheus scrape only (there is no OTLP metrics exporter) and the ClickStack tier brings no Prometheus - accessLog is the path that reaches ClickHouse. The labels cost nothing and are correct for anything that scrapes later.

attributes.description: Extra entries as name -> CEL expression. Guard every claim read with has(): an unauthenticated request has no jwt object at all and an unguarded expression throws. agentgateway allows at most 16 metric labels in total.

enabled.description: false = no metrics policy. The metrics keep being served, just without these labels.

includeTeam.description: The chargeback dimension. One series per team per model, bounded by the number of teams, which is what makes it the safe default.

includeUser.description: HIGH-CARDINALITY: one series per person per model per metric, paid for forever. Off by default - the same attribution is in the access log, which is a row per request instead of a series per user.

platformRoutes.description: exposure.type=Gateway + exposure.gatewayMode=path only: the portal-stack route table the installer computes and injects onto this composition (one entry per exposed component with a gatewayPath — frontend/authn/snowplow/sse-proxy — all on the single platform-http listener at exposure.platformPort). The agentgateway-policies chart programs the listener + one route per entry from it. The installer fills this fill-if-absent, so an explicit override here WINS; leave it unset to let the installer compute it. Inert outside path mode.

backend.description: The ClusterIP Service this route forwards to.

listener.description: The gateway listener this route attaches to.

protocol.description: Listener protocol. Defaults to HTTP when unset. Set HTTPS together with tls to terminate TLS on this listener.

tls.description: TLS termination for an HTTPS listener. When set, the listener emits tls.mode + certificateRefs to the named Secret.

certificateRef.description: Name of the kubernetes.io/tls Secret (same namespace as the Gateway) holding the listener certificate + key.

mode.description: Gateway-API TLS mode. Defaults to Terminate.

name.description: Route name (the routed component's name).

pathPrefix.description: The listener path prefix this route matches (e.g. /auth, /content, /events, or / for the portal origin).

rewrite.description: Whether the gateway strips pathPrefix before forwarding to the backend.

resiliency.description: Retries and timeouts, one policy per hop. The split is the point: a model call is slow by nature and safe to retry, while a tool call is fast and not necessarily idempotent, so retrying one that already reached the tool runs it twice. Retries surface as agentgateway_retries_total.

a2a.description: The A2A hop - the catch-all agent route and every sub-agent route, since a delegated hop is an A2A hop with the same posture.

retry.description: Retry policy for one hop. attempts:0 renders no retry at all.

attempts.description: Extra attempts after the first, so 2 means up to three calls. 0 = no retries.

backoff.description: Base backoff between attempts, e.g. 1s or 500ms.

codes.description: Response codes that are retried. 4xx/5xx only. 429 is deliberately absent from the defaults: it is the upstream telling us to stop.

condition.description: Raw CEL over the RESPONSE deciding retryability, on top of codes. Empty = unused.

precondition.description: Raw CEL over the REQUEST, evaluated before any attempt, so an expensive request can be made non-retryable. Empty = unused.

timeout.description: Empty = no timeout. An A2A call is a whole delegated agent turn, model and tool calls included, so any ceiling here is a ceiling on how long a specialist may think.

enabled.description: false = no retry or timeout policy on any hop; each takes agentgateway's defaults of no retries and no request timeout.

llm.description: The LLM hop. A transient provider 503 currently fails a whole Autopilot turn, which is the case this exists for.

retry.description: Retry policy for one hop. attempts:0 renders no retry at all.

attempts.description: Extra attempts after the first, so 2 means up to three calls. 0 = no retries.

backoff.description: Base backoff between attempts, e.g. 1s or 500ms.

codes.description: Response codes that are retried. 4xx/5xx only. 429 is deliberately absent from the defaults: it is the upstream telling us to stop.

condition.description: Raw CEL over the RESPONSE deciding retryability, on top of codes. Empty = unused.

precondition.description: Raw CEL over the REQUEST, evaluated before any attempt, so an expensive request can be made non-retryable. Empty = unused.

timeout.description: Empty = NO TIMEOUT, deliberately: a model call is slow by nature and a short timeout turns a long generation into a 504 the user reads as a broken agent. Mutually exclusive with llm.http.requestTimeout, which bounds a single provider call rather than the whole route - a render guard rejects setting both.

mcp.description: The proxied MCP hop. Conservative: retry only what plausibly never reached the tool, which is why 504 is absent from the default codes.

retry.description: Retry policy for one hop. attempts:0 renders no retry at all.

attempts.description: Extra attempts after the first, so 2 means up to three calls. 0 = no retries.

backoff.description: Base backoff between attempts, e.g. 1s or 500ms.

codes.description: Response codes that are retried. 4xx/5xx only. 429 is deliberately absent from the defaults: it is the upstream telling us to stop.

condition.description: Raw CEL over the RESPONSE deciding retryability, on top of codes. Empty = unused.

precondition.description: Raw CEL over the REQUEST, evaluated before any attempt, so an expensive request can be made non-retryable. Empty = unused.

timeout.description: A tool call that has not answered in this long is not going to. Bounded, unlike the LLM hop, because a hung tool call holds an agent turn open behind it.

sessionTrace.description: Allows the portal's Evidence panel to read a session's stored activity (GET /api/sessions/...). Read-only.

subjects.description: Who a rule grants access to. The matchers are OR'd; at least one must be set, otherwise the rule would deny everyone. `anyAuthenticated` is IGNORED when `users` or `groups` is set: these blocks are deep-merged maps, so a caller narrowing a rule to a group never sees the default `anyAuthenticated: true` disappear, and OR'ing it back in would silently restore access to everyone. Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

anyAuthenticated.description: Any request carrying a token this gateway validated. Ignored when `users` or `groups` is set.

groups.description: Values that must appear in the groups claim (authn: `groups`, a list of strings).

users.description: Values of the user claim (authn: the username in `sub`).

stt.description: Speech-to-text transcription route (agentgateway-policies stt): /stt/v1 on the TLS platform listener, guardrail-free + Strict-JWT + metered. Set enabled:true to turn on voice input — requires exposure.tls (a TLS platform listener). Off by default in the chart.

enabled.description: Emit the /stt/v1 transcription route + gate + limits. Requires a TLS platform listener.

limits.description: Volume/size bounds on the transcription route (audio bodies are large). Each disables with 0/"".

maxRequestBytes.description: Request body cap in bytes for audio; over => 413. 0 = off.

tokensPerHour.description: Model tokens/HOUR (429 over) — per-hour budget so a long dictation can burst. 0 = off.

routePrefix.description: Path prefix for the transcription route.

subAgents.description: Layer 3 — every agent that can be an A2A delegation target. Each entry renders the header-matched route, the token passthrough, the anonymous agent-card allowance and the delegation rule.

name.description: Agent name, which is also its Service name and the x-kagent-host value.

The matchers are OR'd; at least one must be set, otherwise the rule would deny everyone. `anyAuthenticated` is IGNORED when `users` or `groups` is set: these blocks are deep-merged maps, so a caller narrowing a rule to a group never sees the default `anyAuthenticated: true` disappear, and OR'ing it back in would silently restore access to everyone. Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

anyAuthenticated.description: Any request carrying a token this gateway validated. Ignored when `users` or `groups` is set.

groups.description: Values that must appear in the groups claim (authn: `groups`, a list of strings).

users.description: Values of the user claim (authn: the username in `sub`).

tracing.description: OTel trace export for the whole gateway data plane. When enabled, renders the agentgateway-policies-tracing AgentgatewayPolicy (attached to the Gateway, not a single route) so every route's spans - including the /llm/v1 route's gen_ai.* token attributes - are exported to an OTLP collector, making LLM token/cost observable (ClickStack -> ClickHouse). Default off; needs agentgateway-policies >= 0.1.10.

attributes.description: Extra span fields as name -> CEL expression, on top of agentgateway's own defaults (which already carry the gen_ai.* token attributes). Kept to low-cardinality dimensions rather than payloads: a span attribute rides every span. Guard every claim read with has(): an unauthenticated request has no jwt object at all and an unguarded expression throws.

backendRef.description: OTLP collector Service to export spans to. Must INGEST OTLP: the ClickStack DAEMONSET collector (otel-collector-daemonset-opentelemetry-collector:4317), not the deployment collector (no OTLP receiver on its traces pipeline).

clientSampling.description: Whether to honour a trace decision the CALLER already made. Empty by default: nothing upstream of this gateway propagates a trace context worth honouring, and honouring one would let a caller decide our span volume. A BARE INTEGER OTHER THAN 0 OR 1 IS REFUSED: agentgateway v1.5.0's cel eval_rng clamps an integer to 0..1, so "5" and "100" both mean ALWAYS, not 5% and not 100%. Someone reducing sampling by writing a percentage would silently maximise it. Accepted: "0.05", "1", "0", "true", "1.0" and CEL expressions. Mirrors agentgateway-policies 0.2.20's own schema, so the refusal happens here and not only at render. BOUNDED AT 1024 FOR A REASON THE CHART DOES NOT SHARE: the `not` above compiles into a CEL rule in the generated Installer CRD, and the apiserver's cost estimator multiplies a rule's cost by every unbounded collection above it — an unbounded string makes it assume the maximum and REFUSE the CRD (the 0.3.508 defect; see check-cel-cost-shape). agentgateway-policies' own schema has the same `not` with NO maxLength, which is correct there because helm validates values directly and compiles nothing. 1024 is far beyond any realistic sampling expression — the longest its owner cites is 42 characters — so this bound is stricter than the chart's and can only accept what the chart accepts.

filter.description: CEL gate on whether a SAMPLED span is exported. The default keeps model calls and failures and nothing else: backend.type is 'ai' only on the LLM route, so kubelet probes, anonymous agent-card fetches and the chatty MCP hop are all dropped. Empty = export every sampled span. This is the lever to narrow with - randomSampling drops spans at RANDOM and a randomly-sampled set loses LLM token accounting.

includeToolCalls.description: PAYLOAD-BEARING. llm.toolCalls is on for ACCESS LOGS because a log row is one row per request; a span attribute rides every span and carries the same payload again. Off here so it is not paid for twice.

includeUser.description: HIGH-CARDINALITY: one distinct value per person, on every span. Off - the same attribution is in the access log, which is cheaper per unit of information.

platform.description: Overrides for the PLATFORM Gateway's own tracing policy (gateway.internalDataPlane), agentgateway-policies >= 0.2.19. A key set here REPLACES the shared tracing value for that Gateway only; a key left unset inherits it. The AGENT Gateway is unaffected. Mirrors the chart's own values.schema.json: the five overridable keys and their types are taken from it, not inferred. DELIBERATELY NO DEFAULTS ANYWHERE IN HERE — a `default:` on any of these is written into every existing deployment's Installer CR on the next roll, including installs with no tail sampler, which must keep inheriting `filter` = errors only.

clientSampling.description: As tracing.clientSampling, for the platform Gateway. MUST BE SET BEFORE BROWSER TRACING IS TURNED ON (installer#405): agentgateway v1.5.0's log.rs trace_sampled samples a request ALWAYS when this is unset and the request arrives carrying a traceparent — so the first browser to send one would have every request sampled. "true" with tail sampling, a float ratio without it. A BARE INTEGER OTHER THAN 0 OR 1 IS REFUSED: agentgateway v1.5.0's cel eval_rng clamps an integer to 0..1, so "5" and "100" both mean ALWAYS, not 5% and not 100%. Someone reducing sampling by writing a percentage would silently maximise it. Accepted: "0.05", "1", "0", "true", "1.0" and CEL expressions. filter.description: As tracing.filter, for the platform Gateway. "" exports every sampled span, which is correct ONLY for an install whose collectors tail-sample (otel-collector-tailsampling, observability#118). ORDERED: set this only AFTER otel-collector-daemonset 0.1.20 is live and exporting to the sampling tier. Setting it earlier sends every platform span straight to ClickHouse unsampled.

randomSampling.description: As tracing.randomSampling, for the platform Gateway. READ THE UNITS: agentgateway v1.5.0's cel eval_rng treats a bool as-is, a FLOAT as a probability clamped to 0..1 ("0.05" = 5%), and an INTEGER as clamped to 0..1 too — so "100" means ALWAYS and "5" ALSO means ALWAYS, not 5%. A bare integer meant as a percentage silently maximises sampling. The chart's owner is adding a pattern that rejects bare integers other than 0 and 1; mirror it here when it lands. A BARE INTEGER OTHER THAN 0 OR 1 IS REFUSED: agentgateway v1.5.0's cel eval_rng clamps an integer to 0..1, so "5" and "100" both mean ALWAYS, not 5% and not 100%. Someone reducing sampling by writing a percentage would silently maximise it. Accepted: "0.05", "1", "0", "true", "1.0" and CEL expressions. removeAttributes.description: Default span fields to drop on the platform Gateway. The chart defaults it to [jwt.sub]: the portal path carries no user identity on spans (Diego, installer#398) — "who" is the audit log's job. The AGENT Gateway keeps jwt.sub, because it attributes LLM spend.

resources.description: As tracing.resources, for the platform Gateway.

randomSampling.description: A BARE INTEGER OTHER THAN 0 OR 1 IS REFUSED: agentgateway v1.5.0's cel eval_rng clamps an integer to 0..1, so "5" and "100" both mean ALWAYS, not 5% and not 100%. Someone reducing sampling by writing a percentage would silently maximise it. Accepted: "0.05", "1", "0", "true", "1.0" and CEL expressions. Mirrors agentgateway-policies 0.2.20's own schema, so the refusal happens here and not only at render. removeAttributes.description: Default span field names to drop. Empty = keep them all.

resources.description: Attributes describing the ENTITY that produced the span, as name -> CEL expression. Minimal by default: the collector's k8sattributes processor already adds pod, namespace and node.

tts.description: Text-to-speech speak-back route (agentgateway-policies tts): /tts/v1 on the TLS platform listener, static backend to Google Cloud TTS (EU multi-region, keeps answer text in-region), guardrail-exempt + Strict-JWT + bounded. Set enabled:true to upgrade Autopilot speak-back from the browser voice to Cloud TTS — requires exposure.tls (a TLS platform listener). Off by default in the chart. Pair with the frontend AUTOPILOT_VOICE_TTS_URL (https://<host>/tts/v1/text:synthesize).

enabled.description: Emit the /tts/v1 speak-back route + backend + gate + limits. Requires a TLS platform listener.

host.description: Cloud TTS endpoint host (default the EU multi-region eu-texttospeech.googleapis.com).

limits.description: Volume/size bounds on the speak-back route (the request is small answer text; the response carries the audio). Each disables with 0/"".

maxRequestBytes.description: Request body cap in bytes (answer text is small); over => 413. 0 = off.

routePrefix.description: Path prefix for the speak-back route (default /tts/v1).

upstreamPrefix.description: Path the routePrefix is rewritten to upstream (default /v1, so /tts/v1/text:synthesize -> /v1/text:synthesize).

uiTokenHop.description: The kagent dashboard's authenticating front door. The kagent controller runs AUTH_MODE=trusted-proxy — it identifies a caller only from a bearer and DECODES it without verifying the signature (an alg:none token with any sub returns 200) — while kagent-ui sends no bearer at all. This hop exchanges its own projected ServiceAccount token (audience-bound to authn) for a real RS256 Krateo JWT at authn's intra-service strategy, drops whatever Authorization the client sent, stamps its own, and sends /api through the Gateway so the signature is actually verified. One shared SERVICE identity, not the dashboard user's: it makes the dashboard's identity unforgeable, it does not make the dashboard multi-user. Default OFF — it needs authn, and enabling it also activates networkPolicy.ui.

apiPathPrefix.description: Prefix the hop sends to the Gateway rather than to kagent-ui, and identically the path the Allow clause admits for `identity`. /api/ is the whole controller API, which is what a dashboard needs — including /api/a2a/, which is the chat itself.

audience.description: Enforced by authn via TokenReview; what stops the projected token being replayed elsewhere. Must match authn's AUTHN_SERVICEACCOUNT_AUDIENCE.

loginUrl.description: Empty = derived from the jwt.jwks block, so authn's location is configured once.

tokenExpirationSeconds.description: Kubelet rotation period for the projected token — NOT the minted JWT's lifetime.

create.description: The serviceaccount.authn.krateo.io/ServiceAccount allowlist entry. Without it the exchange 403s. False when managed elsewhere.

namespace.description: authn reads these only from its own operator namespace. Empty = the JWKS Service's namespace.

enabled.description: ON by default: kagent-ui is unusable behind the gateway without it — the controller reads identity only from a bearer and kagent-ui sends none. Set false to drop the hop and its pod.

gatewayUrl.description: Gateway origin for that traffic. Empty = this chart's own Gateway Service, already the catch-all A2A route onto the controller, so no extra HTTPRoute is needed.

groups.description: The issued token's `groups` claim. Bind RBAC to the group rather than the username.

identity.description: The authn allowlist entry's name, which becomes `sub` on every minted token AND the subject the Gateway Allow clause admits. One value drives both so they cannot drift.

pullSecrets.description: IMAGE-pull secrets for the private ui-token-hop image. Auto-wired by the installer from registryAuth (the derived krateo-registry-image-pull dockerconfigjson); set explicitly to override, or [] to opt out. Declaring a schema default here would defeat that: helm materializes it onto the Installer CR and the injection's hasKey test then skips it.

impersonation.description: DEVELOPMENT ONLY. View the kagent dashboard as another user. kagent scopes every session listing to the authenticated principal and exposes no all-users view, so the dashboard lists only what the hop's own shared service identity created; history written under a human login stays invisible. This overrides the user id kagent sees, via the X-User-Id/X-Agent-Name pair its trusted-proxy authenticator prefers over the token's `sub`. The bearer stays the hop's real token, so the Gateway still verifies a genuine signature — only the application-level user id changes. NOT authentication: the viewed user has no relation to whoever is at the keyboard, and anyone who can reach the hop can view as anyone. Needs componentValues.kagent.kagentapp.ui.additionalForwardedHeaders to carry x-user-id and x-agent-name, or it covers direct /api calls only and silently misses the dashboard's Next.js server-action data path.

agentName.description: Fills X-Agent-Name, which kagent requires before it honours X-User-Id at all. Its only other use is a guard on POST /api/sessions/{id}/events, called exclusively by the ADK agent runtime against the controller directly — never through this hop.

allowedUsers.description: Restricts which user ids may be selected. Empty = any.

defaultUser.description: Who to view as when no cookie is set. Empty = the hop's own identity, so enabling the switch alone changes nothing until a user is picked. Flip it per-browser at /_hop/user?set=<id>.

minRefresh.description: Floor between exchange attempts, so a failing authn is not hammered once per request.

skew.description: Re-mint this long before the minted JWT's exp.

agentgateway-policies.title: Agentgateway Policies

agentiko.description: Values for the `agentiko` component, chart `agentiko` (krateo-agentiko). The side-by-side successor to krateo-autopilot during the rename: both are pinned, both are orchestrators, and they share no object name. VERIFIED 2026-11-08: `helm show values` for agentiko 0.8.0 and krateo-autopilot 0.7.3 have IDENTICAL top-level keys, so this entry is autopilot's shape unchanged. The delta is inside `agents`: the orchestrator key is `agentiko` (not `autopilot` — the chart FAILS the render if agents.autopilot is set, proven against the published chart), and agents.k8s/.helm take `owned`. `mcpServers.clickhouse` is no longer read by this chart. `knowledge` has no `enabled`: krateo-knowledge is skipped whenever agents.k8s.owned is false.

agentgateway.description: Re-attach the caller's JWT to this agent's own outbound MCP/A2A calls (KAGENT_PROPAGATE_TOKEN) — what lets per-user tool and delegation RBAC be enforced at the gateway. Set for you on every agent when features.agentGateway is on.
agentgateway.title: Agent gateway

owned.description: Whether THIS release creates and owns the sub-agent's Agent object. false means the orchestrator still delegates to an Agent of this name that ANOTHER release owns — the hand-over state during the krateo-autopilot -> agentiko rename, which is what stops the two releases fighting over the live k8s-agent/helm-agent. Present on agents.k8s and agents.helm in the charts; the orchestrator's own entry has skillRef instead. NO DEFAULT: the charts default it to true, and a default here would be written into every existing deployment's CR on the next roll. DO NOT CONFUSE with `enabled`, which gates the gateway's subAgents ROUTING entry: enabled:false silently stops routing to an Agent that still exists, owned:false hands over an Agent that is still being routed to.

agents.description: Agents to deploy, keyed by agent name. modelConfig is a plain ModelConfig NAME the autopilot chart does not own — the slots come from the model-configs component (gemini-flash, gemini-pro).

extraAgents.description: Extra A2A sub-agents to register on the orchestrator (component/blueprint-contributed specialists, e.g. the installer's installer-agent). The orchestrator stays the single mandatory entry point; these are reachable only via its routing.

extraTools.description: Extra McpServer tool blocks on the autopilot Agent only: each entry binds the named toolNames of an existing RemoteMCPServer CR this chart does not own (kind RemoteMCPServer, apiGroup kagent.dev). Built for the bench profile (e.g. an evidence server). The CR must exist before the Agent; kagent compiles the tool list once.

name.description: RemoteMCPServer CR name.

global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.
global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

hitlApproval.description: HITL approval gate for mutating k8s tools. true=pause for approval (safe); false=autonomous remediation.

knowledge.description: Generic Kubernetes knowledge the krateo-autopilot chart (0.4.8+) appends to the K8S-AGENT's system prompt, one section per enabled file, delivered as the krateo-knowledge ConfigMap. The chart defaults BOTH files to true and this chart sets agents.k8s.enabled=true, so the chart defaults would be LIVE here: ~9,000 words / ~11.7k input tokens on EVERY model call of that agent (the system message is resent per turn and is never compacted). The installer therefore turns both OFF, which is what makes the 0.4.7 -> 0.4.8 pin bump behaviour-neutral: that release is knowledge-only, so with knowledge off the rendered agents are byte-identical to 0.4.7. The object-level default keeps the key present in the schema-defaulted componentValues so a live-values override (playbook:true) durably merges through the self-bootstrap patch instead of being dropped (the previewSandbox mechanism); the per-file defaults keep the OTHER file explicitly off when only one is turned on. Turn them on deliberately, one file at a time, with a measurement either side. Inert on a pin older than 0.4.8: that chart's values.schema.json has no knowledge key, so the generated CRD prunes it silently — which is why the switch-off must land in the SAME change as the pin bump, never after it.

Unset: plain HTTP. Callers trust the issuer's CA through a trust-manager Bundle, NEVER by reading authn's Secret, which holds the private key. jwt.description: authn signs tokens with an RSA private key (RS256) and publishes the matching public key as a JWKS at GET /.well-known/jwks.json. The private key is mounted from a Secret as a file (never injected as an env var).

kid.description: Key ID advertised in every token header and in the JWKS "kid". Must be stable for the lifetime of the key so validators can match it.

signKeySecretKey.description: Key inside that Secret whose value is the PEM private key; it is also the mounted filename.

signKeySecretName.description: Name of the Secret holding the PEM-encoded RSA private key (created by the installer umbrella before authn).

previousKeys.description: RETIRED keys that still VERIFY. NEVER set this by hand: it is DERIVED from authn.jwt.keyGeneration and authn.jwt.overlapGenerations and FORCED onto this component, for the same reason signKeySecretName and kid are. A listed key keeps verifying, while keyGeneration exists to STOP honouring already-issued tokens -- so the two levers are opposites, and set together by hand they produce a rotation that invalidates nothing while every signal reports success: new Secret created, authn Ready, clean boot. That is the failure check-signing-key.py exists for. Declared here only because the forced value must validate against this schema. No default, for the crdgen reason above.

kid.description: Key ID of the retired key, as it appears in the JWKS and in every token that key signed. No comma, equals sign or whitespace: authn receives the entries as kid=path pairs.

secretKey.description: Key inside that Secret holding the PEM. The derivation FORCES private.pem rather than omitting it: authn defaults it to private.pem today, but a derived field that silently tracks another chart's default is the coupling the sibling forced fields avoid.

secretName.description: Secret holding the retired key. authn reads only its PUBLIC half (jwks.ParsePreviousKeys -> publicKeyFromPEM), so a previous key never signs. This Secret must EXIST for as long as it is listed: authn refuses to start otherwise and the pod hangs mounting the volume, so drop the generation from this list BEFORE deleting its Secret.

instances.description: INSTALLER POLICY, NOT A CHART DEFAULT (frontend, 2026-11-13). builder-gate's chart defaults instances to [] because it is opt-in by design; which builders a platform runs is the installer's composition decision, so we default all three. Recorded because this MATERIALIZES into every Installer CR and beats the chart. Audited against builder-gate 1.8.42. controller-render-service.description: The POST /render preview service behind the Controller Builder. It runs the oasgen-provider IMAGE with the /bin/oasgen-render entrypoint, so its version IS oasgen's version -- it is a member of the `oasgen` line in .github/pin-version-lines.yaml, not an independent chart. Only the two keys below are declared: this node did not exist before, so nothing of this chart was ever settable from the installer and no CR can be carrying anything else. Widening later is always possible; narrowing is not.

maxBodyMiB.description: Largest POST /render body accepted, in MiB. THE CONTAINER'S MEMORY LIMIT IS DERIVED FROM THIS and must not be set independently -- parsing holds roughly 29x the document live at peak, so a cap raised without memory is a service that accepts bodies it cannot render (oasgen#628). At 64 MiB the derived limit is already ~2.4Gi for a SINGLE request. The bounds mirror the chart's own schema; the chart's `default: 4` is deliberately NOT mirrored, because crdgen materialises an installer-schema default into the Installer CR where it beats the chart's values.yaml -- a later change to the chart default would then be silently ignored on every cluster. A mirrored CONSTRAINT can only reject; a mirrored DEFAULT becomes a value.

memoryLimitOverride.description: Replaces the derived memory limit entirely. Empty, the chart's default, means derive from maxBodyMiB. Setting it reopens the coupling the derivation exists to close, so set it only after measuring the workload; oasgen-render still refuses to start if the cap exceeds what the limit can cover. No installer default, for the same reason as above.

dashboard-page.description: The dashboard-page chart, one of the fifteen page charts split out of the portal shell at 1.8.80 (portal#261/#323). It creates its own namespace and renders only into it, because `resourceNames` cannot narrow `list`: the namespace is the only boundary page visibility has. Every key here is an OVERRIDE of the chart's own values.yaml and carries NO `default:` -- crdgen propagates a chart schema default into the generated composition CRD, where the apiserver materialises it into the leaf CR spec and the chart's values.yaml never runs (measured at 1.8.78: the marketplacepages CRD defaulted readerGroups to [admins] and the live CR carried it with nothing having written it). So leave a key UNSET to take the chart's value; `namespace` and `readerGroups` both come from the chart unless an install needs to move a page or grant another group.

namespace.description: The namespace this chart CREATES and installs its page objects into. It is the RBAC boundary the chart exists for — a group with no RoleBinding here cannot `list` the page roots, so the portal sidebar never shows them and the page body 403s on a deep link. The release itself stays in the portal's namespace (the shell), and only these objects live here.
namespace.title: namespace

readerGroups.description: Groups granted read of these pages in `namespace`. A group listed here sees /dashboard in the sidebar and can open it; a group absent cannot list the page roots, so the entry never renders. No schema default: the installer applies schema defaults, so one here would silently re-assert itself over a group set through componentValues. The chart default lives in values.yaml instead.
readerGroups.title: readerGroups

external-dns.description: Spec for the external-dns edge component (feature: ingress), deep-merged into its Composition. Mirrors oci://ghcr.io/krateo-blueprints/charts/external-dns 0.3.x: config lives under the `external-dns` subchart-passthrough key (0.2.0 exposed these at the top level where they never reached the workload — a breaking-shape fix). The provider API token is referenced via `env[]` from an out-of-band Secret, never part of the blueprint.

The chart marks `external-dns` root-required with domainFilters, txtOwnerId and env required inside it. The default is on THIS object, not only on its children: structural-schema defaulting fills fields of objects that are PRESENT, so child defaults never apply when the parent is absent and the CR is rejected for the missing required key. Values copied from the chart's own values.yaml — the chart defaulting them does NOT satisfy the generated CRD, because crdgen keeps `required` and the CR's spec is built from componentValues (installer#489).
