agentName.description: Which kagent Agent the portal talks to. The frontend chart drives BOTH modes from this one key: with the agentgateway on it appends /api/a2a/<namespace>/<agentName>, and with it off the relative base becomes /<agentName> unless config.AUTOPILOT_API_BASE_URL or config.AGENTIKO_API_BASE_URL is set explicitly, which still wins. LEAVE UNSET to keep the frontend chart's own default, which is `agentiko` from 1.8.34. Bounds match the FRONTEND CHART'S OWN schema exactly (pattern + maxLength 63), deliberately: a wider bound here would accept a value the component chart then refuses, moving the error from this schema to a cdc reconcile where it is far harder to read. Set it only to HOLD a cluster on a specific agent across a frontend bump whose default differs -- which is why this key exists: without it, pinning a frontend release whose default is `agentiko` would move the portal off `autopilot` as a side effect of a routine pin, performing a migration step nobody approved.

agentgateway.description: Route the portal's Autopilot A2A calls through the agentgateway data plane instead of straight to kagent-ui, so the user Bearer they carry is validated and per-user RBAC applies. Injected fill-if-absent from features.agentGateway. NO `default` ON `enabled`, DELIBERATELY — see below.

enabled.description: MUST NOT CARRY A `default`. compositions.yaml fills this with true via inst.fillPath (fill-if-ABSENT) when features.agentGateway is on, and core-provider applies this schema's defaults into the Installer CR spec — so `default: false` here is not documentation, it is a value that pre-occupies the key and silently blocks that fill. It shipped that way: every install with the gateway on served the bare gateway origin as AUTOPILOT_API_BASE_URL, the frontend chart appends /api/a2a/<ns>/autopilot only when this is true, so the rail POSTed to / and every Autopilot turn failed with 405. check-fill-defaults.py fails CI if a default returns on any fill-if-absent target.

kinds.description: Which of the 32 GitHub RestDefinitions this component renders. EMPTY OR ABSENT RENDERS ALL 32 and is byte-identical to 0.7.3, so this carries NO DEFAULT -- a seeded list would silently narrow every install, and a default on any installer schema property propagates into the live CR. A child sets a subset to avoid roughly 32 rest-dynamic-controller pods against a 100-pod tenant quota. Needs the pin at 0.7.4 or later: the field does not exist in 0.7.3's schema. WARNING: omitting Repository or PullRequest while the github-provider-kog-config component is enabled leaves that chart unrenderable -- `deps` and `requiresApiGroups` both pass, because the component is Ready and the API group exists, so nothing catches it except the render guard in definitions.yaml.

identity-lifecycle.description: Full-coverage override surface for the identity-lifecycle chart (pinned 0.1.4). Every key of the chart's values.yaml is typed here and nothing is left open: componentValues is additionalProperties:false and CI (check-no-unknowns.py) fails any PR reintroducing additionalProperties:true or x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields. `resources`, `podSecurityContext` and `securityContext` are type:object with NO additionalProperties in the chart's own schema -- neither false nor true, so permissive -- and acmp confirmed neither chart means to accept arbitrary fields, so they are closed here to exactly the keys their values.yaml sets. `extraEnv` items are bare type:object upstream and are closed here to the EnvVar shape.

accessRequest.description: VERBATIM COPY of identity-lifecycle 0.4.1's own values.schema.json properties.accessRequest, taken from the published chart. Copied rather than hand-listed because the subtree has 84 leaves and a hand list would drift from the chart silently -- componentValues.identity-lifecycle is additionalProperties:false, so a leaf we miss is PRUNED with kubectl still printing "patched". Checked before copying: the subtree is additionalProperties:false throughout, declares NO `required` (so it cannot wedge the umbrella render) and carries NO `default:` (so nothing materializes into every Installer CR). Re-copy it from the chart on the next identity-lifecycle bump rather than editing it here. The AccessRequest controller, the decided-by policy and the public intake. Off by default.

caBundle.description: The CA bundle identity-lifecycle presents when calling authn over TLS (AUTHN_CA_FILE). NEW in identity-lifecycle 0.4.2. On a cluster with internal TLS this is trust-manager's distributed bundle: {configMap: krateo-internal-ca, key: ca.crt} -- trust-manager writes that ConfigMap into IL's release namespace, so the namespaces it targets must include it. THE EMPTY configMap IS ALLOWED ON PURPOSE: the pattern's outer (...)? accepts "", which is the chart's own default meaning no bundle. A pattern that rejected "" would make that default unwritable -- keycloak-provider-kog caught that before I tightened it. NO DEFAULT and NO REQUIRED, matching the source chart, which has neither anywhere in this node. THE CHART REFUSES TO RENDER when configMap is set with an http:// accessRequest.authn.url, so a bundle configured against a plaintext endpoint fails loudly rather than being silently unused.

k8sAnalyze.description: Deterministic first pass — k8s_analyze, config-refs-mcp-server's second tool (CR owned by that chart, a coreAgents component): it lists a namespace's live objects plus Nodes, runs pure-function condition checks and returns typed findings instead of raw dumps, so the same cluster state always yields the same findings in the same order. Read-only. Default false — new and unmeasured, so it ships as the control arm of an A/B, like repoSearch.graph above. Needs config-refs-mcp-server 0.2.4 or later, the release that first serves the tool; on anything older kagent drops the unserved name silently and the binding is inert. Set it only once the incident-agent pin carries the binding: that chart's own values.schema.json is closed (additionalProperties: false), so an older pin rejects the key outright.

knowledge.description: The same generic Kubernetes knowledge as componentValues.krateo-autopilot.knowledge, here appended by the incident-agent chart (0.1.9+) to the incident-agent's OWN system prompt and delivered as the incident-agent-knowledge ConfigMap. No agents.* gate stands in front of it, so at the chart's true/true defaults it is unconditionally live: ~9,000 words / ~11.7k input tokens on every model call. Turned OFF here, which is what makes the 0.1.8 -> 0.1.9 pin bump behaviour-neutral — that release is knowledge-only, and with both files off the chart renders no knowledge ConfigMap and an Agent byte-identical to 0.1.8. Object-level default so the key survives the schema-defaulted componentValues expansion and a live-values override merges durably; per-file defaults so turning one file on leaves the other explicitly off. Inert on a pin older than 0.1.9 (no knowledge key in that chart's schema, so the generated CRD prunes it), which is why the switch-off ships in the SAME change as the pin bump.

retention.description: How long a Closed or Resolved incident is kept after status.resolution.at, as a Go duration. NO DEFAULT HERE, DELIBERATELY, and that is a change from how this key was first added in #990. This node's own description states the rule: a default on a componentValues leaf is applied into the live composition spec by core-provider, so it is a SILENT OVERRIDE rather than documentation. #990 gave this key `default: "0s"` and that broke the rule -- it would have kept injecting 0s into every cluster's CR even after the values entry was removed, so removing the override alone would NOT have produced the 720h Diego chose, and I would have reported a change that had not happened. With no default here and no entry in values.yaml, the chart's own default applies: 720h, 30 days. Diego decided 2026-11-16, confirmed directly. THE SWEEP IS A PERMANENT DELETE on the first reconcile at component >=0.12.0. Measured on krateo-057: 232 incidents (96 Closed, 86 Resolved, 49 Open, 1 Verifying); 31 have status.resolution.at older than 720h, oldest resolved 1010h ago. Open and Verifying are never touched. RECOUNT BEFORE THE ROLL -- it grows as incidents resolve. Shortening this later deletes immediately and irreversibly on the next reconcile, so any change is its own decision and roll. The chart's path is controller.retention; see #1004 for why the top-level `retention` this repo used to send was rejected rather than ignored.

settleWindow.description: How long, from entering Verifying, a verify exit 1 is retried before the incident goes back to Open.

incidents-page.description: The incidents-page chart, one of the fifteen page charts split out of the portal shell at 1.8.80 (portal#261/#323). It creates its own namespace and renders only into it, because `resourceNames` cannot narrow `list`: the namespace is the only boundary page visibility has. Every key here is an OVERRIDE of the chart's own values.yaml and carries NO `default:` -- crdgen propagates a chart schema default into the generated composition CRD, where the apiserver materialises it into the leaf CR spec and the chart's values.yaml never runs (measured at 1.8.78: the marketplacepages CRD defaulted readerGroups to [admins] and the live CR carried it with nothing having written it). So leave a key UNSET to take the chart's value; `namespace` and `readerGroups` both come from the chart unless an install needs to move a page or grant another group.

namespace.description: The namespace this chart CREATES and installs its page objects into. It is the RBAC boundary the whole chart exists for — a group with no RoleBinding here cannot `list` the page roots, so the portal's sidebar never shows them and the page body 403s on a deep link. The release itself stays wherever the composition is created (krateo-system on the platform install); only the page objects live here. Changing it after install orphans the previous namespace's objects, which Helm will not prune because it no longer renders them.
namespace.title: namespace

readerGroups.description: Groups granted read of these pages in `namespace`. A group listed here sees /incidents in the sidebar and can open it; a group absent cannot list the page roots, so the entry never renders. `devs` is deliberately NOT a default — keeping it out is the point of the split (#261). No schema default: the installer applies schema defaults, so one here would silently re-assert itself over a group set through componentValues. The chart default lives in values.yaml instead.
readerGroups.title: readerGroups

serviceDeskNamespace.description: Namespace the incidents page reads the service-desk ticket queue from (portal 1.8.109, #410/#411). NO default here on purpose: a default in this file is written into the Installer CR and becomes a silent live override. The chart's own values.yaml defaults it to krateo-service-desk, which is correct on 057 (read from the cluster), so nothing needs to set this today -- it is declared so it CAN be set, because this node is additionalProperties:false and an undeclared key is silently pruned with every check green. If the key is absent the Tickets card reads the chart default; on an install with no service desk that 404s and the card hides.

database.description: Bundled-Postgres storage sizing for kagent. Fully typed (additionalProperties: false) per check-no-unknowns; A DEFAULT IS REQUIRED or the nested key is dropped from schema-expansion and never reaches the component release (installer #173/#174). The default matches the kagent chart's own 500Mi so it is a no-op for every install that does not override it. WHY THIS EXISTS: a PVC can only ever GROW. If an operator expands the live PVC (e.g. to recover a full disk) while the chart still declares the smaller size, helm's self-heal apply tries to patch it DOWN, the apiserver rejects it, and the kagent composition is stuck Synced=False FOREVER. That is not a local failure: the installer umbrella then reports Ready=False 'managed children not healthy', and Pass B's deps-Ready gate stops emitting EVERY component that depends on kagent -- on krateo-057 that silently left 8 agent components with no composition CR at all while their pods kept running unmanaged. Declare the real size here whenever the live PVC is resized.

storage.description: PVC size for the bundled kagent Postgres (chart default 500Mi). MUST match the live PVC size: Kubernetes forbids shrinking a PVC, so declaring less than what exists wedges the kagent composition Synced=False and, via the umbrella's deps-Ready gate, blocks emission of every kagent-dependent component. krateo-057 runs 8Gi after the 2026-09-15 disk-full recovery.

kagent-tools.description: Gate for upstream kagent's kagent-tools sub-chart (the cluster-admin tool server). Set {enabled:false} together with perUserRbac.enabled=true to run tools under per-user RBAC instead; setting one alone is a hard template-time failure in the kagent chart. Declared WITH a default so the installer's componentValues schema-default expansion keeps the key — an undeclared nested key is dropped and the override never reaches the release.

enabled.description: Render upstream's kagent-tools sub-chart. Leave true unless perUserRbac.enabled is also true.

kagent-tools.title: Upstream kagent-tools sub-chart gate

ui.description: The kagent dashboard, a DEVELOPMENT tool: a real install normally turns it off. NOTE the knob is `replicas: 0`, not an `enabled` flag — upstream kagent renders the UI Deployment/Service/ServiceAccount/ConfigMap unconditionally and ships NO ui.enabled gate (checked in 0.9.12 and in the latest 0.10.1), so an `enabled` key here would validate and then be silently ignored. `replicas: 0` removes the pod — no memory, no attack surface — and leaves the inert Service/ConfigMap behind. Default 1 (the UI is on). Turning it off also makes agentgateway-policies' uiTokenHop pointless: disable both together.

additionalForwardedHeaders.description: Extra request headers the kagent-ui pod forwards to its backend, on TOP of the always-forwarded Authorization. Upstream reads this as KAGENT_ADDITIONAL_FORWARDED_HEADERS. Needed by agentgateway-policies' uiTokenHop.impersonation: the hop stamps X-User-Id and X-Agent-Name on the request, but the dashboard's real data path is a Next.js SERVER ACTION running inside this pod, which re-creates the upstream request and copies only allowlisted headers — so without [x-user-id, x-agent-name] here the switch covers direct browser /api calls only and silently does nothing for the session list. Hop-by-hop headers are dropped by kagent-ui regardless of what is listed.

backendInternalUrl.description: What the kagent-ui pod's Next.js server dials for its SERVER ACTIONS — how the dashboard actually fetches data (POST / with a next-action header), as opposed to the browser's own /api calls. Upstream defaults it to the controller, which agentgateway-policies' containment blocks, so with uiTokenHop on the dashboard loads and then fails every action with "fetch failed". Point it at the gateway: http://<gateway>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:<port>/api. The server action forwards the caller's Authorization (upstream always does), which is the token the hop stamped, and the gateway verifies it. Injected fill-if-absent when componentValues.agentgateway-policies.uiTokenHop.enabled is true.

replicas.description: 0 = the dashboard is off (Deployment scaled to zero). Upstream default 1.

ui.title: kagent dashboard (kagent-ui)

Declared WITH a default so the installer's componentValues schema-default expansion keeps the key — an undeclared nested key is dropped from the expansion and the override never reaches the release.

keycloak.description: Values for the keycloak component. Deliberately minimal: the realm's own configuration (identity provider, authentication flows, required actions, group mappers) is NOT set here -- it is reconciled from keycloak-config-kog CRs, so there is nothing to declare for it. The database comes from the blueprint's defaults plus CloudNativePG. Only values the installer must set per cluster belong here, and an undeclared key is pruned silently with every CI check green.

db.description: REQUIRED ON THE COMPOSITION CR. keycloak 0.2.3's values.schema.json carries a root-level `required: [keycloak, db]`, which crdgen turns into mandatory fields on the Keycloak Composition CR. The umbrella emits that CR carrying only what componentValues supplies -- the chart's own values.yaml defaults do NOT populate it -- so omitting `db` makes the apiserver reject the object with `spec.db: Required value`, and because that rejection happens inside the Installer composition's own helm reconcile it stalls EVERY component, not just Keycloak. Measured on krateo-demo 2026-11-11 at 0.3.582: Installer went Synced=False/ReconcileError with 108 managed children frozen. The proper fix is for the keycloak chart to drop the root `required` (its values.yaml already carries full defaults); this node exists so the installer is not wedged while that lands, and remains useful afterwards for overriding the database wiring.

backup.description: CNPG backup configuration for the Keycloak database, from keycloak 0.4.1. Absent leaves the chart default, which configures no backup.

className.description: VolumeSnapshotClass for CNPG volume-snapshot backups of the database (e.g. a pd.csi.storage.gke.io class on GKE). Empty = no backup configuration, which is the chart default. The class itself is cluster infrastructure and is NOT rendered by the chart, so it must exist before this is set. Emptying the value removes spec.backup from the CNPG Cluster, proven live by keycloak-provider-kog, so the knob is reversible.

hostname.description: The externally reachable base URL Keycloak issues tokens for. MUST be set per cluster: the chart's default is the placeholder https://keycloak.example.com, and an issuer that does not match the URL users actually reach makes every OIDC validation fail. On krateo-demo it has to match the hand-installed TLS edge, so it is a per-cluster value rather than a chart default.

relativePath.description: Serve Keycloak under a path prefix (Keycloak's http-relative-path), e.g. /keycloak: starts with /, no trailing slash; keycloak.hostname must then END with it or the chart refuses to render. Empty is the chart default and means the root. NEW IN keycloak 0.4.0 -- the operator CRD has no native field for it, so the chart renders it as a Keycloak option. REQUIRED on a gatewayMode=path cluster: exposure.hosts and exposure.baseDomain are HOST-MODE ONLY, so Keycloak cannot be given a subdomain while gatewayMode is path, and the issuer its tokens carry must stay stable whatever path a request arrives on. On krateo-057 that means hostname https://portal.krateo.dev/keycloak with relativePath /keycloak.

tlsSecretName.description: Names a Secret the installer does NOT create. On krateo-demo the TLS edge is hand-installed, so this points at an object whose lifecycle is outside this chart.

instances.description: Keycloak replica count. Defaulted in values.yaml.

name.description: The Keycloak CR's name. Structural, not environmental -- defaulted in values.yaml, not here: a default in this file would be written into the Installer CR itself.

auth.description: Admin authentication for the KOG. On demo it runs in BOOTSTRAP mode against the Secret keycloak-bootstrap-service that the keycloak blueprint creates. Bootstrap is a SUB-MODE of externalSecret -- the ExternalSecrets and the Webhook generator render only when externalSecret.enabled is true -- so externalSecret.enabled is deliberately NOT declared here: forcing it false would mean nothing mints a token. Left absent, tokenEndpoint and bootstrap.namespace are derived from namespaces.krateo by inst.componentValuesResolved, because the chart defaults name keycloak-system and Krateo installs compositions into namespaces.krateo.

enabled.description: Use the keycloak blueprint's bootstrap service account instead of a pre-provisioned client credential. Defaulted true in values.yaml: it is a mode choice, not namespace-dependent.

namespace.description: Namespace holding Secret keycloak-bootstrap-service, i.e. the Keycloak namespace. The chart `required`s it whenever bootstrap is enabled, so a missing value FAILS the render rather than misbehaving quietly. Derived from namespaces.krateo when absent.

tokenEndpoint.description: The Webhook generator URL the KOG mints its admin token from. CONSULTED IN BOOTSTRAP MODE TOO -- bootstrap changes only the credential source, not the token URL. Derived when absent.

baseUrl.description: REQUIRED ON THE COMPOSITION CR. keycloak-config-kog 0.5.2's values.schema.json has root `required: [keycloak]` and nested `keycloak.required: [baseUrl]`, so the Composition CR is uncreatable without it and the rejection freezes the whole umbrella. Left ABSENT it is derived by inst.componentValuesResolved as http://keycloak-service.<namespaces.krateo>.svc.cluster.local:8080 -- NOT the chart's own default, which names keycloak-system while Krateo installs compositions into namespaces.krateo. Set it explicitly only to point at a Keycloak outside the cluster.

restDefinitions.description: Which RestDefinitions the KOG emits. Mirrors the chart's restDefinitions, declared as the UNION of its values.yaml and its own values.schema.json: the chart's schema omits `user` while its values.yaml sets it, and this node is additionalProperties:false, so declaring only the schema's eleven would leave restDefinitions.user unexpressible. No `default:` on any leaf -- a default here materializes into the CR and would freeze the chart's own value.

Lifecycle verbs are delegated to Snowplow RESTActions because Keycloak has no set-replace call for role mappings and addresses both the service-account user and the role-owning client only by UUID. keycloak-operator.description: Values for the keycloak-operator component. Deliberately minimal: only what a cluster may need to override. The chart's own defaults are watchNamespaces=krateo-system, startupProbe.failureThreshold=3, image.tag=26.6.3 and keycloakImage=26.6.3, and those are left to the chart. Declared at all because componentValues is a closed object -- before this node existed, ANY value for this component was pruned silently with every CI check green, which made a measured startupProbe recommendation unimplementable rather than merely unset.

failureThreshold.description: startupProbe.failureThreshold for the operator pod. The chart ships 3, about 35 s, and keycloak-provider-kog measured the JVM operator being KILLED by it under load on kind; they recommend around 30. Raise it on a cluster where the operator starts slowly. This is a liveness-shaped value, so getting it wrong presents as a CrashLoopBackOff that looks like a broken image rather than a probe that fired too early.

watchNamespaces.description: watchNamespaces for the operator, which the chart maps to the Quarkus KEYCLOAKCONTROLLER and KEYCLOAKREALMIMPORTCONTROLLER namespace env vars. Defaults to krateo-system, where the realm lives today. Set it only if Keycloak or KeycloakRealmImport CRs must be reconciled in other namespaces -- a per-tenant realm would need it, and without widening it the operator SILENTLY IGNORES CRs outside krateo-system rather than erroring.

krateo-audit-worm.description: Tamper-evident WORM mirror of the krateo_audit table, with a hash-chained seal and a verifier (component krateo-audit-worm, gated on features.auditWorm). Renders one ConfigMap and two CronJobs: no helm hooks and no lookup, so a helm-template render-diff sees every object the chart will create. The seal CronJob owns the ClickHouse schema and applies it idempotently on every run, failing loudly until the krateo_audit table exists. Table and image names are deliberately NOT exposed here: they are internal to the chart, and the verifier's correctness depends on the seal and the mirror agreeing about them.

clickhouse.description: Where the audit table lives. Defaults come from the chart, which points at the krateo-observability ClickHouse instance.

credentialsSecret.description: Secret carrying the ClickHouse user and password, read via secretKeyRef. The credentials are never rendered into the Composition spec.

global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.
global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

seal.description: The CronJob that mirrors new audit rows into the WORM table and extends the hash chain.

lagSeconds.description: How far behind now() to stop sealing, so rows still arriving for the current window are not sealed into a chain link they would later contradict.

verify.description: The CronJob that re-walks the hash chain and reports integrity. Goes RED on a broken chain, a dropped materialized view, or a dropped/truncated seal table.

staleAfterSeconds.description: Age past which an unextended chain is reported as stale. A verifier that only fails on a BROKEN chain cannot tell a healthy quiet period from a seal CronJob that stopped running.

krateo-audit-worm.title: krateo-audit-worm values

krateo-autopilot.description: RETIRED COMPONENT, KEPT ONLY SO A LIVE CR CAN DRAIN. krateo-autopilot was unpinned by 0.3.606 (#849) and its real 404-line node deleted in the same change. That made the render FAIL CLOSED for any cluster whose CR still carried this key: `at '/componentValues': additional properties 'krateo-autopilot' not allowed`, because componentValues sets additionalProperties:false. krateo-demo carried it (agents, knowledge), so its catch-up roll would have been refused. This node re-declares the key as a bare object so helm accepts whatever a CR already holds; it is an untyped object on purpose, because the values it has to tolerate no longer have a maintained shape. crdgen therefore emits x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields for it, so the contents are PRESERVED, not pruned -- the key does NOT drain by itself, and clearing it is an explicit CR merge patch setting componentValues.krateo-autopilot: null. The hole is registered in check-no-unknowns.py's DECLARED_OPEN with that reason. Nothing reads it — with no pin there is no release. Deliberately NO `default`, which would materialize the key into every CR that does not have it (installer-schema-defaults-propagate-to-cr). Remove this node and the files/retired-components.yaml entry TOGETHER, in one commit, once no live CR carries either; check-retired-components.py enforces the pairing. Set nothing here: use componentValues.agentiko, the successor.

tenantAdmin.description: The tenant's role in their own namespace. Renders three Kyverno policies (policies.kyverno.io/v1). A GeneratingPolicy binds each tenant user, in their own namespace, to <aggregationRoles.namePrefix><defaultRole>, or to the role an admin lists for them in the ConfigMap <rolesConfigMap.namespace>/<rolesConfigMap.name> (data `<user>: <role>`). A ValidatingPolicy keeps that ConfigMap's entries to the catalog's roles, and a MutatingPolicy re-evaluates every tenant namespace when it changes. Kyverno's background controller needs `bind` on each role it may bind (policies/kyverno/kyverno-values.yaml).

enabled.description: Render the tenant role binding, its ConfigMap guard and its resync policy
enabled.title: enabled

defaultRole.description: Role a tenant user gets in their own namespace when the ConfigMap lists no other. One of aggregationRoles.roles[].name.
defaultRole.title: defaultRole

bindingNamePrefix.description: Prefix of the RoleBinding generated in each tenant namespace; the role name follows it (krateo-tenant-admin, krateo-tenant-auditor, ...). One name per role, because a RoleBinding's roleRef cannot change.
bindingNamePrefix.title: bindingNamePrefix

rolesConfigMap.description: The ConfigMap where an admin lists another role for a tenant user (data `<user>: <role>`). Tenants cannot write it.
rolesConfigMap.title: rolesConfigMap

tenantReader.description: Tenant read access to the resources a tenant's compositions manage. Renders the aggregating ClusterRole <aggregationRoles.namePrefix><roleName>, a Kyverno GeneratingPolicy that binds it with a namespaced RoleBinding in every tenant namespace, and a Kyverno ValidatingPolicy that keeps it read-only and Secret-free (policies.kyverno.io/v1). Requires Kyverno 3.9.2 (v1.19) installed with policies/kyverno/kyverno-values.yaml (the controller permissions these policies need).

bindingName.description: Name of the RoleBinding generated in each tenant namespace. Changing it on a live install is not covered by the tests; reinstall the chart instead, which only recreates these RoleBindings.
bindingName.title: bindingName

enabled.description: Render the tenant reader role, its binding policy and its guard policy
enabled.title: enabled

policyNamePrefix.description: Prefix of the two Kyverno ClusterPolicies (<prefix>binding and <prefix>guard)
policyNamePrefix.title: policyNamePrefix

roleName.description: Aggregation name of the tenant reader role. Charts grant tenants read access to the kinds they manage by labeling a capability ClusterRole rbac.krateo.io/aggregate-to-<roleName>=true (or listing <roleName> in a capability's aggregateTo).
roleName.title: roleName

tenantNamespaceLabel.description: Namespace label that marks a tenant namespace (value "true"), as set by the tenant onboarding policy
tenantNamespaceLabel.title: tenantNamespaceLabel

tenantUserLabel.description: Namespace label that carries the tenant's user name; the RoleBinding subject is User:<value>. Namespaces without it get no binding.
tenantUserLabel.title: tenantUserLabel

krateo-capability-roles.description: Values for krateo-capability-roles. Deliberately MINIMAL: only the one key a cluster must be able to change is exposed. Every other chart value (capabilities, capabilityRoles.namePrefix, aggregationRoles, composer, and the rest of tenantReader) stays at the chart default, which is what krateo-demo runs today — helm get values returns null there. NOTE: these nodes are additionalProperties:false, so a key that is not declared here is silently PRUNED on its way to the composition; widen the schema in a tag BEFORE anything sets a new key.

krateo-keycloak-realm.description: Overrides for krateo-keycloak-realm. Every object here is a keycloak-config-kog custom resource, so this component renders nothing until the KOG has generated its CRDs -- which is what requiresApiGroups keycloak.ogen.krateo.io gates on. The key list is keycloak-provider-kog's final one for 0.1.0; resourceGroup is deliberately NOT exposed, because it names the API group the KOG generates into and belongs to keycloak-config-kog, not to a per-install override. NO `default:` anywhere below: a default here would propagate into the Installer CR and become a silent live override. The chart's own values.yaml carries the defaults instead.

clients.description: Confidential relying parties (e.g. Keystone), one KeycloakClient each, with a generated client secret. New in krateo-keycloak-realm 0.5.0. The item-level `required` is retained from the chart and is safe: array items may require their own keys, because the requirement is only evaluated for items somebody wrote.
clients.title: Additional confidential clients

configuration.description: The per-kind <Kind>Configuration the KOG controllers authenticate with, pointing at the bearer-token Secret keycloak-config-kog rotates.

tokenSecret.description: Read from the release namespace, so no cross-namespace Secret access is needed. Install this component where keycloak-config-kog keeps the token.

deletionPolicy.description: What happens IN KEYCLOAK when one of this chart's resources is deleted (helm uninstall, a prune, a kubectl delete). orphan (the chart default): the Kubernetes object goes and the realm, its groups and the client stay in Keycloak untouched, so a mistaken prune cannot wipe the realm and every user in it; a reinstall adopts them again. delete: set it explicitly only to really decommission the realm.

groups.description: Top-level realm groups. Membership is managed by the joiner flow, never here. Names are emitted verbatim in the groups claim, so they must not start with "/" (that is a group PATH) or "system:" (reserved by Kubernetes).

attributes.description: Keycloak group attributes, typed as its REST API types them: each key maps to a LIST of strings, so a bare string value is rejected. The chart passes this through verbatim.

ideClient.description: The PUBLIC client IDEs (Claude Code, Cursor) sign in with to reach the platform's MCP endpoint: authorization code + PKCE S256, loopback redirects, preferred_username, the portal's groups claim, and `audience` in the access token's aud. New in krateo-keycloak-realm 0.5.0. Chart defaults it OFF, so there is no transient-on window on the roll that introduces it.

audience.description: The MCP resource the gateway expects in the access token's aud, BYTE-FOR-BYTE, e.g. https://portal.krateo.dev/mcp (https, lowercase host, path /mcp, no trailing slash). The chart's description calls it "REQUIRED when enabled, no default" while its schema carries default: "" -- reported upstream; treat it as required-when-enabled and set it explicitly.
audience.title: MCP audience

clientId.description: The IDE's --client-id and the MCP gateway's clientId. Chart default krateo-ide.
clientId.title: Client ID

enabled.description: Render the IDE client. Chart default false.
enabled.title: Enabled

groupsClaim.description: Token claim carrying bare group names, as for the portal client. Chart default groups.
groupsClaim.title: Groups claim

name.description: Shown on the consent and login pages. Chart default "Krateo IDE (MCP)".
name.title: Display name

redirectUris.description: Loopback redirects; the IDE opens the port (RFC 8252 7.3). Chart default [http://localhost:*, http://127.0.0.1:*].
redirectUris.title: Redirect URIs

ideClient.title: IDE client

identityLifecycle.description: identity-lifecycle's own client for access requests: confidential, service account only, secret generated once into a Secret it mounts, and its service account holding EXACTLY `roles` of `roleClientId`. Needs keycloak-config-kog >= 0.8.0 for the role-mapping RestDefinition. Chart defaults it OFF.

enabled.description: Render the client, its secret and the role mapping. Chart default false.
enabled.title: Enabled

roleClientId.description: clientId of the client that owns the roles. Chart default realm-management.
roleClientId.title: Role client

roles.description: EXACTLY the roles of roleClientId the service account holds; a role added by hand is removed. Chart default [manage-users, view-users, query-groups].
roles.title: Roles

secret.description: The Secret the client secret is generated into, in the release namespace (identity-lifecycle's accessRequest.keycloak.clientSecretRef).

key.description: Key of the client secret in it. Chart default clientSecret.
key.title: Secret key

name.description: Name of the generated Secret. Chart default identity-lifecycle-idp.
name.title: Secret name

secret.title: Client secret

identityLifecycle.title: identity-lifecycle client

oidcConfig.description: Added by krateo-keycloak-realm 0.2.0, which emits authn's OIDCConfig alongside the realm. The realm chart owns it deliberately: the OIDCConfig must agree with the realm on issuer, clientID, redirectURI and the allowed groups, and all four live in this same chart -- templating it installer-side would duplicate them and drift into a login that returns a token the portal rejects. The object renders ONLY where authn's oidc.authn.krateo.io/v1alpha1 API exists (.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has), so a cluster without authn does not block the realm. Key names and casing mirror the chart exactly, including discoveryUrl with a lowercase 'rl' -- the chart reads discoveryUrl and renders it into the CRD's discoveryURL, and 'correcting' it here would silently stop the value reaching the release.

allowedGroups.description: Realm groups permitted to sign in. Empty or unset means every group name in the realm.

discoveryUrl.description: Override for the discovery document URL. Leave UNSET when Keycloak is publicly exposed over HTTPS, which is the supported posture: authn then discovers on the public host over TLS with system CAs. Do NOT point this at plain in-cluster http -- authn does not verify ID-token signatures (it relies on receiving the token directly from the token endpoint over TLS, OIDC Core 3.1.3.7), so an unauthenticated in-cluster exchange would let anything able to tamper with cluster traffic mint an ID token with groups [platform-admins]. In-cluster https with a private-CA cert that authn trusts is the safe alternative.

graphics.description: Presentation of the sign-in button in the portal's strategy list.

keycloakUrl.description: The PUBLICLY reachable Keycloak base URL, which becomes the issuer together with the realm name. It must be the host the user's BROWSER reaches, not an in-cluster Service: the browser is redirected there and validates the token's issuer claim. Derive it from the same source as componentValues['keycloak'].keycloak.hostname and keep the two identical.

name.description: Name of the OIDCConfig object. The portal's strategy list keys off it.

oidcConfig.title: authn OIDCConfig emitted by the realm chart

parentClient.description: The portal's OIDC client: public (no secret), authorization code + PKCE S256, with a groups claim carrying bare group names. clientId must match the value authn's OIDCConfig uses.

postLogoutRedirectUris.description: A STRING, unlike redirectUris and webOrigins which are arrays. The chart default is "+", meaning the redirect URIs are reused.

redirectUris.description: Required in practice when parentClient is enabled: the chart defaults it to an EMPTY list, which the schema permits, so a client with no redirect URI installs cleanly and then cannot complete a login.

actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan.description: Lifetime of administrator-sent action links (the set-password email), in SECONDS. 259200 is 72 hours.

adminEvents.description: ADMIN event recording — a SIBLING of `events`, not a field inside it (confirmed against the released 0.3.1 schema rather than inferred, because declaring it one level deep would be pruned silently). New in krateo-keycloak-realm 0.3.1. Both keys are left WITHOUT a default so the chart's own defaults (enabled true, includeRepresentation false) govern; see the note on events.expiration.

enabled.description: Record admin events (realm/client/user changes made through the admin API). The chart defaults this to TRUE, so pinning 0.3.1 turns admin-event recording on by itself — that is the chart owner's decision, deliberately not overridden here. Set false to keep the pre-0.3.1 behaviour.

includeRepresentation.description: Store the full JSON representation of the changed object with each admin event. Chart default false. Turning it on writes complete object bodies into the Keycloak event store, so it grows the realm database and can capture configuration values; treat it as a data-retention decision, not a verbosity knob.

expiration.description: How long Keycloak keeps USER events, in SECONDS. New in krateo-keycloak-realm 0.3.1; the chart defaults it to 7776000 (90 days). NO DEFAULT HERE on purpose: a `default:` in this schema is written into every Installer CR by the self-bootstrap patch, which would stamp a retention period onto clusters that never chose one and freeze the chart's ability to change its own default (installer-schema-defaults-propagate-to-cr). Inert on a pin older than 0.3.1: that chart's values.schema.json has no such key, so the generated CRD prunes it silently — which is why this widening ships BEFORE the pin bump, never after.

registrationAllowed.description: Self-registration. Off in the demo design: accounts are created only through an administrator-approved joiner flow.

rememberMe.description: Show "Remember me" on the Keycloak sign-in page. A ticked session gets a persistent cookie and rememberMeSessions' timeouts; unticked sessions are unchanged. The chart's own default is false (Keycloak's default). NO SCHEMA DEFAULT HERE, deliberately -- the installer applies schema defaults onto the Installer CR, so a default would silently re-assert itself over an operator's choice. KEY NAME CHECKED AGAINST THE CHART, not against Keycloak: the realm CR spec field the template produces is also `rememberMe`, but its two timeout fields are NOT -- see rememberMeSessions.
rememberMe.title: rememberMe

rememberMeSessions.description: SSO timeouts in SECONDS for sessions signed in with Remember me ticked. 0 means use the realm's ordinary SSO timeouts. THE KEY NAMES HERE ARE THE CHART'S, NOT THE CR'S: the chart reads `rememberMeSessions.idleTimeout` and `.maxLifespan` and its template renders them as the KeycloakRealm spec fields `ssoSessionIdleTimeoutRememberMe` and `ssoSessionMaxLifespanRememberMe`. Declaring the CR-spec names here instead would have produced a node the chart never reads -- settable, silently inert, and APPARENTLY fixed, which is worse than a refusal. REMOVING THESE KEYS LATER IS NOT A NO-OP: dropping them from the values file is inert (RFC-7386 omission preserves), but a componentValuesUnset renders false/0/0, which is one realm PUT that actively turns Remember me OFF.
rememberMeSessions.title: rememberMeSessions

smtp.description: Outgoing mail. Off by default: an install without SMTP gets a realm that sends nothing, and the realm, groups and client still reconcile -- only sending fails.

auth.description: A STRING enum, not a boolean. Keycloak stores these realm flags as strings, so `true` unquoted is rejected.

authType.description: basic: SMTP AUTH with a password. token: XOAUTH2 with an OAuth2 client-credentials token (Keycloak >= 26.2), required by providers that disable password SMTP AUTH, e.g. Microsoft 365.

credentialsSecret.description: The SMTP credentials as keys of ONE Secret in the release namespace, placed by the operator of the cluster and never carried in chart values. userKey is the SASL user in both modes; passwordKey is used by authType basic, clientSecretKey by token.

port.description: A STRING, not an integer -- this is the chart's type and Keycloak's realm field is a string. 587 must be quoted.

ssl.description: A STRING enum, not a boolean.

starttls.description: A STRING enum, not a boolean.

users.description: Users the realm chart creates, as KeycloakUser objects reconciled through the chart's KeycloakUserConfiguration. NO PASSWORDS: a first password is set by the user through Keycloak's "Forgot password?" flow using realm SMTP. Kept on uninstall. Mirrors the realm chart's own schema, so a value this accepts cannot be one the chart then rejects at render.

name.description: The KeycloakUser object's own name, when it must differ from the chart's default of <realm>-<username>. Needed to ADOPT a pre-existing object rather than create a second one beside it: demo's personas are objects named persona-ada/-bob/-acme/-globex whose usernames are ada/bob/acme/globex, and the originals carry the default delete policy, so a duplicate pair per user is not a cosmetic problem. Optional; omit it on a fresh install.
name.title: KeycloakUser object name

username.description: Length bounds mirror the realm chart's own user-profile validation (krateo-keycloak-realm 0.6.2, files/keycloak-26-default-user-profile.json: min 3, max 255). Keycloak refuses a shorter username with a 400 AT CREATE, not at render or apply, so a looser bound here moves the rejection into a reconcile where the offending field is not in the message.

users.title: Realm users

resources.description:
Resources is the resource requirements for the server container.
Applied as a whole: operator defaults are used only when all resource fields are empty.

claims.description:
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims,
that are used by this container.

This field depends on the
DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers.

items.description: ResourceClaim references one entry in PodSpec.ResourceClaims.

name.description:
Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of
the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available
inside a container.

request.description:
Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim.
If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise
only the result of this request.

limits.description:
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

requests.description:
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified,
otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

dataVolumeClaimSpec.description: Specification of persistent storage for ClickHouse data.

accessModes.description:
accessModes contains the desired access modes the volume should have.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#access-modes-1

dataSource.description:
dataSource field can be used to specify either:
* An existing VolumeSnapshot object (snapshot.storage.k8s.io/VolumeSnapshot)
* An existing PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim)
If the provisioner or an external controller can support the specified data source,
it will create a new volume based on the contents of the specified data source.
When the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate is enabled, dataSource contents will be copied to dataSourceRef,
and dataSourceRef contents will be copied to dataSource when dataSourceRef.namespace is not specified.
If the namespace is specified, then dataSourceRef will not be copied to dataSource.

apiGroup.description:
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

kind.description: Kind is the type of resource being referenced

name.description: Name is the name of resource being referenced

dataSourceRef.description:
dataSourceRef specifies the object from which to populate the volume with data, if a non-empty
volume is desired. This may be any object from a non-empty API group (non
core object) or a PersistentVolumeClaim object.
When this field is specified, volume binding will only succeed if the type of
the specified object matches some installed volume populator or dynamic
provisioner.
This field will replace the functionality of the dataSource field and as such
if both fields are non-empty, they must have the same value. For backwards
compatibility, when namespace isn't specified in dataSourceRef,
both fields (dataSource and dataSourceRef) will be set to the same
value automatically if one of them is empty and the other is non-empty.
When namespace is specified in dataSourceRef,
dataSource isn't set to the same value and must be empty.
There are three important differences between dataSource and dataSourceRef:
* While dataSource only allows two specific types of objects, dataSourceRef
  allows any non-core object, as well as PersistentVolumeClaim objects.
* While dataSource ignores disallowed values (dropping them), dataSourceRef
  preserves all values, and generates an error if a disallowed value is
  specified.
* While dataSource only allows local objects, dataSourceRef allows objects
  in any namespaces.
(Beta) Using this field requires the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.
(Alpha) Using the namespace field of dataSourceRef requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

apiGroup.description:
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

kind.description: Kind is the type of resource being referenced

name.description: Name is the name of resource being referenced

namespace.description:
Namespace is the namespace of resource being referenced
Note that when a namespace is specified, a gateway.networking.k8s.io/ReferenceGrant object is required in the referent namespace to allow that namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant documentation for details.
(Alpha) This field requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

resources.description:
resources represents the minimum resources the volume should have.
Users are allowed to specify resource requirements
that are lower than previous value but must still be higher than capacity recorded in the
status field of the claim.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#resources

limits.description:
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

requests.description:
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified,
otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

selector.description: selector is a label query over volumes to consider for binding.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

items.description:
A label selector requirement is a selector that contains values, a key, and an operator that
relates the key and values.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description:
operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values.description:
values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic
merge patch.

matchLabels.description:
matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

storageClassName.description:
storageClassName is the name of the StorageClass required by the claim.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#class-1

volumeAttributesClassName.description:
volumeAttributesClassName may be used to set the VolumeAttributesClass used by this claim.
If specified, the CSI driver will create or update the volume with the attributes defined
in the corresponding VolumeAttributesClass. This has a different purpose than storageClassName,
it can be changed after the claim is created. An empty string or nil value indicates that no
VolumeAttributesClass will be applied to the claim. If the claim enters an Infeasible error state,
this field can be reset to its previous value (including nil) to cancel the modification.
If the resource referred to by volumeAttributesClass does not exist, this PersistentVolumeClaim will be
set to a Pending state, as reflected by the modifyVolumeStatus field, until such as a resource
exists.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-attributes-classes/

volumeMode.description:
volumeMode defines what type of volume is required by the claim.
Value of Filesystem is implied when not included in claim spec.

volumeName.description: volumeName is the binding reference to the PersistentVolume backing this claim.

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node.
Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/

items.description:
The pod this Toleration is attached to tolerates any taint that matches
the triple <key,value,effect> using the matching operator <operator>.

effect.description:
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects.
When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.

key.description:
Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. Empty means match all taint keys.
If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys.

operator.description:
Operator represents a key's relationship to the value.
Valid operators are Exists, Equal, Lt, and Gt. Defaults to Equal.
Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a pod can
tolerate all taints of a particular category.
Lt and Gt perform numeric comparisons (requires feature gate TaintTolerationComparisonOperators).

tolerationSeconds.description:
TolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be
of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint. By default,
it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and
negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system.

value.description:
Value is the taint value the toleration matches to.
If the operator is Exists, the value should be empty, otherwise just a regular string.

settings.description: ClickHouseCluster spec.settings. Declared so ClickHouse USERS are expressible through the installer at all -- before this there was no path: cluster.spec declared only containerTemplate/dataVolumeClaimSpec/podTemplate/replicas/shards behind additionalProperties:false, so adding a user meant a hand edit to the cluster CR that the cdc reverts. Found on the A0 test day, where an OpenStack usage emitter and showback each needed their own scoped principal and there was no way to give them one.

extraUsersConfig.description: Extra ClickHouse users, rendered into the cluster's users config. The CRD types this as x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields, so the shape is ClickHouse's own.

grants.description: Grant statements applied to this user. EXACTLY ONE ITEM, and maxItems enforces it: each list item becomes its own <grants> element in ClickHouse's preprocessed users.xml, and CLICKHOUSE READS ONLY THE FIRST, SILENTLY. Measured on krateo-057 at installer 0.3.532 — a chops user declared with 8 separate items received exactly one grant (SELECT ON system.disks) while both the Installer CR and the pod's 99-extra-users-config.yaml held all 8. The user logged in and every other check passed, so nothing failed: it was simply under-privileged, and a refusal for lack of a grant is indistinguishable from a refusal by design. Put every privilege in ONE statement, comma-separated, as the built-in `app` user does: "GRANT SELECT ON system.disks, SELECT ON system.parts, ALTER DELETE, ALTER MATERIALIZE TTL ON default.otel_logs". Reported as observability#117.

password_sha256_hex.description: sha256 hex of the user's password. The pattern is enforced so a plaintext password cannot be put here by mistake -- a cleartext value will fail schema validation rather than silently become a credential in the CR.

users.description:
username -> user definition. USE password_sha256_hex, NOT password.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN STYLE. The component chart's own defaults are PLAINTEXT literals (hyperdx.secrets.CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "otelcollectorpass", CLICKHOUSE_APP_PASSWORD: "hyperdx") and the chart offers no secret reference for them -- its only *SecretName knob is mongodb's scram. A `password:` set here therefore travels as cleartext into the Installer CR, into etcd, and into the helm release Secret, readable by anything with get on them. `password_sha256_hex` is a verifier rather than a secret and is ClickHouse's native field for exactly this, so it is what this knob is for. The installer's own credential-reference pattern (registryAuth.passwordRef, a name/namespace/key Secret ref) is NOT available here, because the chart templates the password as a plain string into the cluster CR and resolves no ref. Making a ref work is a krateo-observability chart change.

SCOPE THE GRANTS. `INSERT ON default.*` includes default.krateo_audit, so a third-party writer granted it can insert rows that krateo_audit_worm_mv hashes and seals as genuine -- a forgery path through the tamper-evidence the audit trail exists to provide. Grant per table, never per database, for anything that is not the audit writer itself.

config.description: Opaque passthrough into the upstream clickstack hyperdx.config map (rendered into the clickstack-config ConfigMap). In Gateway path mode the installer computes FRONTEND_URL from the gateway origin (fill-if-absent); an explicit value here wins. No schema default (schema-defaults rule).

ttlDays.description: Must exceed the 30-day SLO window by at least a day. RAISED 29 -> 31 WITH THE 0.1.3 PIN, to match the chart: krateo-slo-rollup 0.1.3's own values.schema.json sets minimum 31, because the 30d statements in ops/slo-alert/sli-span-metrics.sql read 30 whole UTC days before today, so a TTL of 29 or 30 could expire the window's first day before it is read. LEAVING THIS AT 29 WOULD HAVE BEEN A DRIFT IN THE PERMISSIVE DIRECTION: the Installer CRD would accept 29 or 30, the apiserver would store it, and the chart would then refuse to render -- measured, `--set rollup.ttlDays=30` on 0.1.3 fails with "at '/rollup/ttlDays': minimum: got 30, want 31" while 0.1.2 accepted it. Nothing sets it today (chart values null, and 057's CR carries no krateo-slo-rollup values at all), so this closes a latent trap rather than fixing a live break. The chart default of 40 is unchanged and satisfies both.

Read by secretKeyRef, which cannot cross namespaces, so the Secret must live in the sse-proxy release's OWN namespace -- krateo-system on 057 and demo, where krateo-observability creates it. The chart defaults all three keys correctly (clickhouse-sse-proxy-credentials / username / password), so this carries NO default here and only needs setting on a cluster that departs from them. kyverno.description: Per-cluster overrides for the kyverno blueprint. The RBAC the krateo ClusterPolicies need is NOT here — it is defaulted by the wrapper chart from 3.9.4, because every krateo install running those policies needs the same 18 rules and each operator was otherwise rediscovering them. This node is only for what legitimately differs per cluster.

NOTE THE DOUBLE `kyverno`, and that it is not a typo: the wrapper chart's own top level is CLOSED to `global` and `kyverno`, and `.kyverno` is its passthrough to the upstream subchart. So componentValues.kyverno.kyverno.<x> is the only path that reaches upstream; a single-`kyverno` path is refused at CHART LOAD, which is loud and therefore safe. Verified against the wrapper's own values.schema.json rather than assumed.

THIS NODE IS OPEN, which is a deliberate exception to this file's closed-object convention, for two reasons. First, it mirrors the wrapper's own `.kyverno`, which is open for the same reason: upstream kyverno's values schema is enormous and a closed duplicate here would be a maintenance fiction that silently falls behind every upstream release. Second, under a CLOSED node the Installer CRD PRUNES an undeclared key silently — the value vanishes, `kubectl` still prints "patched", and the chart default wins; open preserves it instead. The cost is that a typo here is passed through rather than rejected, so it surfaces as an upstream chart error at render time rather than at the CR write.

The known case is backgroundController.resources (the wrapper defaults 2Gi/256Mi from saas's file). NO `default:` anywhere under this node: a default on a componentValues leaf materializes into every install's live CR — which is why 057's Installer CR still carries four http://localhost:808x strings today.

BOUNDS MIRROR nightly-review 0.2.6's OWN values.schema.json exactly, read from the pinned chart rather than inferred: a wider bound here accepts a value the chart then refuses, which moves the error from this schema to a cdc reconcile where it is far harder to read. The chart defaults (krateo-agent-gateway, the release namespace, 8080) are already correct on every cluster today, so nothing needs to set this -- it is declared because `reviewer` is additionalProperties:false on BOTH sides, so until the key exists here an override is PRUNED BY THE APISERVER while the write reports success. The role named here must hold SELECT on `session` and nothing else: conversation content lives in event.data and task and the role is revoked on both, so the limit is a database privilege rather than a promise the code makes. Verify it where the role is created (session=t, event=f, task=f) rather than trusting these keys. ^clickhouse/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$.description: A NAMED clickhouse exporter instance, e.g. `clickhouse/audit`. Same shape as the unnamed `clickhouse` beside it, enforced by $ref -- verified against helm's own validator: a bad `ttl` unit is rejected THROUGH the ref, and a typo like `clickhoose/audit` is still refused because additionalProperties stays false. It exists so ONE signal can get its own table and its own retention instead of sharing the single `ttl` with every other signal this collector exports: each signal's exporter creates only its own signal's tables at start(), so two instances with different `ttl` values yield two tables with different retention. Set the table name explicitly on the instance and reference it from config.service.pipelines.<signal>.exporters by the same name. This is the FIRST $ref in this schema. The CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS caveat in the sibling ttl description applies to a named instance identically.

ttl.description: RETENTION. Go duration stamped as a native TTL into the otel_* tables the exporter CREATEs (otel-collector-deployment >=0.3.3 / -daemonset >=0.1.5 default it to 168h = 7d). Left unset the chart default applies -- this key carries NO schema default on purpose, so declaring retention is an explicit act and never a silent live override. CAVEAT, read before setting it: create_schema issues CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, so this value only takes effect on tables that do not exist yet. On an install whose otel_* tables already exist (any cluster that has ingested once) changing it is a NO-OP and the live retention stays whatever the tables were created with -- that needs ALTER TABLE <t> MODIFY TTL, which no chart does. Verify with SHOW CREATE TABLE otel_logs before believing this field. 0s is accepted and means NO TTL at all, i.e. unbounded.

clickhouse.description: The chart's schema makes `clickhouse` root-REQUIRED with `address` and `database` required inside it. THE DEFAULT IS ON THIS OBJECT, not only on its children, and that distinction is load-bearing: Kubernetes structural-schema defaulting fills fields of objects that are PRESENT, so defaults on address/database alone would never be applied when `clickhouse` itself is absent — and the CR would be rejected for the missing required key. core-provider applies schema defaults into the Installer CR spec, so this object materialises with both keys when an install sets no componentValues. The per-child defaults are kept so a partial override (just `address`) still yields a valid `database`.

The short name resolves same-namespace, and components deploy into namespaces.krateo. The service is HEADLESS — it has no cluster IP, so this resolves to pod addresses.

OTEL_LOGS_ENABLED.description: Gate the AUDIT-LOG pipeline specifically: snowplow's AuditEvent (internal/support/audit, D19a) emitted as a trace-correlated OTLP LogRecord carrying enduser.id, user.name and user.roles from the AUTHENTICATED caller. DEFAULTS to the value of OTEL_ENABLED when unset, and the snowplow chart therefore ships it EXPLICITLY "false" even with the OTEL_ENABLED master on -- because until otel-collector-daemonset 0.1.11 the agent's logs pipeline had no `otlp` receiver, so an OTLP log export had no consumer and was dropped silently. That is fixed: 0.1.11 adds a dedicated `logs/audit` pipeline writing the `krateo_audit` table with its own 365-day TTL, so records no longer land on the 7-day TTL shared with every pod log. Setting this to "true" is what actually starts the server-authored audit trail (installer#408); it is the LAST step of that chain, and the identity it records is the thing the browser-authored AuditRecord CRs have never carried.

That is why chart/values.yaml carries a componentValues.zendesk-kog.zendesk.baseUrl default: it guarantees the key is always present at render time. Copied verbatim from the chart's own values.schema.json at tag 0.2.4, which has 0 `required` and 0 `default` at any depth, so an empty organisations list never blocks an umbrella render and nothing is materialised into the Installer CR. An incomplete entry fails rendering with a message naming it, which is the chart's own guard rather than a schema one. The access token Secret is created by an administrator in the organisation's namespace; the chart only names it.

tokenRotation.description: Schedule and lifetimes of the External Secrets Operator token rotation.

zendesk.description: The Zendesk instance and the public OAuth client the tokens were authorized with; used by token rotation only.

zendesk-organisations.title: Zendesk organisations

agentiko-mcp-server.description: agentiko-mcp-server: the v1 IDE + personal-agent MCP entry. MIRRORS THE PUBLISHED CHART'S OWN values.schema.json AT 0.2.0 FIELD FOR FIELD, read from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-agentiko/charts/agentiko-mcp-server:0.2.0 rather than from its main, because a bound this schema accepts that the pinned chart then refuses moves the error from a readable schema message to a cdc reconcile. THE WHOLE OBJECT IS MIRRORED, NOT THE `events` NODE ALONE: both sides are additionalProperties:false, so any key declared here-but-not-there is refused by the chart, and any key there-but-not-here is PRUNED BY THE APISERVER while the write reports success. In particular `auth` must be settable, because `events.enabled` requires `auth.mode=exchange` -- declaring only `events` would make the feature impossible to turn on. ZERO `default:` AT ANY DEPTH, verified against the published file by walking it: crdgen propagates schema defaults into the generated CRD, where the apiserver materialises them into every install's Installer CR. The chart declares none either. SHIPS IN ITS OWN TAG, BEFORE THE PIN (installer tag A). The widening is inert -- no component renders from it -- so it rolls at essentially no risk and can be verified on its own; the two pins and features.agentikoMcpServer follow in tag B. If the mirror is imperfect, that is found against a tag that changed nothing else.

global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)
global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.

namespace.description: Namespace the Deployment, Service and ServiceAccount are installed in.
