imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets for the private image.

name.description: Empty means the chart name.

replicaCount.description: The server is stateless; scale freely.

url.description: Agentiko's A2A endpoint. Empty means derived from gateway, namespace and name.

name.description: The Agentiko Agent's name.

namespace.description: The Agentiko Agent's namespace. Empty means .Values.namespace.
Empty means .Values.namespace.

agentiko.description: Where Agentiko's A2A endpoint is: through the internal agent gateway, so each call is authorized as the calling user.

defaultSeconds.description: How long a tool call follows a task when the caller gives no wait_seconds.

maxSeconds.description: Cap on a caller's wait_seconds; must be at least defaultSeconds.

resources.description: Container resources (standard Kubernetes shape).

mode.description: passthrough: the IDE sends an authn JWT. exchange: the IDE sends a Keycloak access token, traded at authn's /delegate (authn#155).

url.description: authn's /delegate. Empty means derived from service, namespace and port.

namespace.description: authn's namespace. Empty means .Values.namespace.

audience.description: The aud asked for the issued authn token.
Audience of the projected ServiceAccount token presented to authn.

create.description: Render authn's delegation mapping for this ServiceAccount (exchange mode).

mapping.description: oidcConfig AND subjectAudiences ARE DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED HERE, and `mapping` is additionalProperties:false, so setting either is REFUSED by this schema rather than pruned. The chart's own values.yaml states the contract: both are derived under the Krateo installer from componentValues.krateo-keycloak-realm (oidcConfig.name and ideClient.audience) and are "not a componentValues key of this chart: setting it there is refused at chart load". WHY REFUSING MATTERS RATHER THAN ALLOWING AN OVERRIDE: the chart requires subjectAudiences[0] to equal krateo-keycloak-realm's ideClient.audience and agentgateway-policies' mcpEntry.oauth.audience BYTE FOR BYTE, no trailing slash, and records that a mismatch fails sign-in with 401 WHILE EVERYTHING REPORTS READY. A second place to set a value that must agree can only ever disagree, and the disagreement is silent. Same shape as componentValues.cert-manager-issuers.internalCA.namespace, which is also refused for being derived. THE DERIVATION DOES NOT EXIST YET, and that is why this is written down rather than assumed: compositions.yaml contains no reference to oidcConfig, subjectAudiences or ideClient as of 2026-11-21, so the chart documents installer behaviour the installer has not implemented. Consequence, stated plainly: with these keys unsettable and no derivation, auth.mode=exchange CANNOT be enabled through the installer -- the chart's own fail in authn-mapping.yaml aborts the render when either is empty, and a chart render failure aborts the WHOLE umbrella. That is the correct state for now (exchange waits on kc-roll057/ideClient anyway) and it fails LOUDLY at render rather than quietly at sign-in. The derivation must be implemented, with forcePath into the component's own spec, BEFORE exchange mode is turned on anywhere.

auth.description: How the IDE user's token becomes the one Agentiko sees.

events.description: Personal-agent events (MCP Events webhook profile). Needs auth.mode=exchange and the agentiko-mcp-server-crds chart.

namespace.description: Namespace of the EventSubscriptions and their signing-key Secrets; it must hold nothing else. Required when enabled.

portalURL.description: The portal's public address, for event links. Required when events are enabled.

readerGroups.description: Groups that may read each events RESTAction (mirror each portal page's readerGroups).

componentValues.title: Per-component spec overrides

componentValuesUnset.description: Dotted paths under componentValues to REMOVE from the live Installer CR, e.g. authn.env.AUTHN_DUMP_ENV. Needed because components-patch.json is applied as an RFC-7386 merge patch: an OMITTED key is PRESERVED — which is what protects operator-set values from a chart upgrade — and only an explicit null deletes. A null cannot be written in the values because the schema types these fields, so without this key a componentValues entry could be set and changed but NEVER removed, and a temporary override became permanent. Measured on krateo-057 2026-11-07: nine components held live componentValues explained by neither the values file nor a schema default. A path whose parent is absent is a no-op, so re-running is safe. NO DEFAULT: a default on any installer schema property propagates into the live CR.

components.description: Advanced. Each entry, matched by `name`, either OVERRIDES a pinned component (whitelisted fields: version / repo / chart / registerOnly / tier — e.g. registerOnly:true to demote a pinned component to registered-but-not-installed, installer#38; or `repo` (+ `chart` for a differing artifact name) to pull that component's chart from a DIFFERENT registry so the source need not be equal for all components, installer#84 — for a re-source to a different registry use registryAuth.registries[] mode so the override gets its OWN pull credential, not the global one) or APPENDS a new registerOnly catalog blueprint. Only `name` is required — an override needs just the field it changes; an append needs kind+version (enforced at render).

agent.description: This component DEPLOYS a kagent Agent. Drives four things at once: the .vertexAI injection (the pod's ADC env / SA-key mount), the HITL approval gate, agentgateway.enabled, and membership of the orchestrator's auto-derived extraAgents fleet. Not set on model-configs, which renders ModelConfigs but no Agent — see modelOwner.

agentName.description: The A2A route name this component's agent is reachable as on the agentgateway, when it differs from the component name. Only meaningful with `agent: true`. For an `orchestrator: true` component the template used to emit the LITERAL "autopilot"; it now reads this key and falls back to "autopilot", so every existing pin renders byte-identically. REQUIRED once two orchestrators are pinned side by side (the autopilot->agentiko rename): without it both emit the same subAgents[].name, producing one duplicate entry and NO route for the second agent. DELIBERATELY HAS NO DEFAULT: a `default:` on any key here is written into every existing deployment's Installer CR on the next roll.

alsoFeatures.description: ADDITIONAL feature flags that also enable this component (ANY-of with `feature`), for a SHARED DEPENDENCY several features need. cloudnative-pg is Keycloak's database and will be kagent's: gating it on `keycloak` alone would mean enabling Keycloak to get a Postgres operator, and moving it to a dedicated feature alone would turn it off underneath the Keycloak already using it. Deliberately an array of string and NOT a oneOf on `feature`: this node feeds crdgen verbatim and becomes the Installer CRD structural schema, and crdgen keeps only the first type of a union. It answers only whether the component MAY be enabled; what must be healthy first is `deps`.

apiRef.description: Pass-through to the generated CompositionDefinition's spec.apiRef — a RESTAction whose calls are resolved each reconcile, keyed under .api in the projection root. TYPED TO MATCH core.krateo.io/v1alpha1 CompositionDefinition EXACTLY (name+namespace, both required, both minLength 1), read from the live CRD rather than guessed: an open object here would let a typo through the installer and be rejected by the apiserver at apply time. spec.apiRef.extras is deliberately NOT exposed — it is free-form, nobody has asked for it, and adding it would reintroduce an untyped escape. Only meaningful on a registerOnly catalog blueprint, whose CompositionDefinition this chart owns. NO DEFAULT: a default on any installer schema property propagates into the live CR. FLOOR: snowplow >= 1.12.38 — per #504 a CompositionDefinition carrying spec.apiRef cannot reconcile on ANY snowplow 1.12.3x below that, so the field is BROKEN rather than inert and fails in a layer that looks unrelated.

name.description: Name of the referenced RESTAction.

namespace.description: Namespace of the referenced RESTAction.

chart.description: Chart artifact name overriding the component name in the OCI URL (e.g. krateo-snowplow). The component name stays the CompositionDefinition/Composition identity; only the chart path changes.

chartRepo.description: CompositionDefinition spec.chart.repo — classic helm repo NAME (only for non-OCI helm-repo charts; OCI components don't need it).

ciRepo.description: The repository whose CI check-pin-ci asserts for this component, as owner/name. When set it is the ONLY repo consulted and the chart's `sources` are not used for resolution. EXPLICIT and never inferred, like `upstream`: a chart's `sources` is free-form metadata, so a dependency or an API spec listed there can carry a coincidentally-matching tag and the gate then asserts an unrelated repo's CI. Resolution inside this repo keeps the normal precedence, chart version before appVersion.

frontendConfigEnv.description: Opt-in: env var key to inject into this component's spec.env with the frontend config-vars ConfigMap name, COMPUTED from the consumer (frontend) component (see compositions.yaml). Used by snowplow's Phase-1 nav-prewarm walker.

gatewayAuth.description: exposure.type=Gateway + gatewayMode=path only: the listener-route auth posture in the platformRoutes entry — public (no token required; login and static portal assets) or optional (a token is verified when present but not required; snowplow content + sse-proxy events). Threaded into the platformRoutes entry as auth.mode.

gatewayListener.description: exposure.type=Gateway + gatewayMode=path only: the agentgateway listener this component's route attaches to. Defaults to the shared platform-http listener; a root-asset app that cannot be path-prefixed (HyperDX) sets its OWN listener (platform-hdx). Threaded into the platformRoutes entry as listener.name.

gatewayPath.description: exposure.type=Gateway + gatewayMode=path only: the listener path prefix this component is routed at through the agentgateway on the single platform listener (frontend /, authn /auth, snowplow /content, sse-proxy /events). compositions.yaml emits it into agentgateway-policies spec.platformRoutes and, for the consumer's peer config URL, appends it to the gateway origin (http://<gw-ip>:<platformPort><path>). Ignored in host mode and for LoadBalancer/NodePort.

gatewayPaths.description: Several path prefixes for ONE component, when a single prefix would expose more than intended. Mutually exclusive with gatewayPath, and the render FAILS if both are set rather than picking one -- choosing silently is how the wrong prefix becomes public. Each prefix renders its own route named <component>-<index>; a single-prefix component keeps its bare name, so the four portal routes are byte-identical.
gatewayPaths.title: gatewayPaths

gatewayPathsFrom.description: Names a DERIVATION that computes this component's path prefixes, instead of literal paths. Mutually exclusive with both gatewayPath and gatewayPaths. `keycloakRealm` builds [<relativePath>/realms/<realm>/, <relativePath>/resources/] from componentValues.keycloak.keycloak.http.relativePath and componentValues.krateo-keycloak-realm.realm.name. It exists because hard-coding those prefixes would repeat the coupling this change fixes for the KOG URLs: rename the realm or move the relative path and the route silently stops matching while every composition stays Ready. Deriving route, baseUrl and tokenEndpoint from the same two values makes them agree by construction. `accessRequestIntake` routes identity-lifecycle's access-request intake, and renders no route when accessRequest.intake is off. An unknown value fails the render loudly.
gatewayPathsFrom.title: gatewayPathsFrom

gatewayPort.description: exposure.type=Gateway + gatewayMode=path only: the port of this component's gateway listener (and, when the component has no exposePort, its route backend port). Defaults to exposure.platformPort. Threaded into the platformRoutes entry as listener.port. HyperDX uses 3000.

gatewayRewrite.description: exposure.type=Gateway + gatewayMode=path only: whether the agentgateway strips gatewayPath before forwarding to the backend Service (true when the backend serves at / — authn/snowplow/sse-proxy; false for the frontend whose gatewayPath is / already). Threaded into the platformRoutes entry as `rewrite`.

graphToggle.description: Dotted path in this component's chart values to the boolean that turns on the repo-mcp-server domain-graph/OKF layer for it (server: graph.enabled; consumers: mcpServers.repoSearch.graph.enabled / repoSearch.graph.enabled). features.repoGraph forcePaths `true` here, in lockstep across every component that declares it. Off => never written.

internalPorts.description: Port-only sibling of internalUrls: an INTEGER port the chart hardcodes at an exposed peer's default — e.g. agentgateway-policies' jwt.jwks.port. Recomputed to exposure.port under the same gate.

path.description: Dotted path in the component chart's values to overwrite.

internalUrls.description: Internal (ClusterIP) URLs this component's chart hardcodes at a peer's per-component default port — e.g. snowplow's env.URL_AUTHN, sse-proxy's auth.urlAuthn. When exposure.port collapses the browser-facing Services onto one shared port those hardcoded ports go dead, so compositions.yaml recomputes each URL on the shared port.

path.description: Dotted path in the component chart's values to overwrite.

peer.description: Service name of the peer the URL points at.

internalPeerUrls.description: In-cluster BASELINE peer URLs this component's chart needs but does NOT default — the missing third mechanism of installer#578. Distinct from the two that exist: `configKeys` derives a BROWSER-reachable address (LB IP, node IP, external hostname), wrong for a controller dialling from inside the cluster; `internalUrls` only CORRECTS an already-present URL onto exposure.port and is gated on $isLB, so it never fires under Gateway — measured on 057 and demo, where both are type Gateway and snowplow's live CR carries no URL keys at all. This one SUPPLIES the value, in every exposure mode. Consumers: oasgen-provider's rdc (URL_SNOWPLOW/URL_AUTHN, whose absence makes *ApiRef delegation silently inert), core-provider's cdc (URL_AUTHN, core-provider#251 item 4), and cmp-usage-collector (showback.url, whose chart FAILS at pure defaults). NOT a schema `default:` — a default on a componentValues leaf lands in every install's CR, which is why 057's Installer CR still carries four http://localhost:808x strings.

path.description: Dotted path in the component chart's values to write the URL to, e.g. rdc.env.URL_AUTHN.

peer.description: COMPONENT name of the peer. Its Service is taken from that component's own `svcMatch` and its port from `exposePort`, never by name-matching: authn also publishes <release>-internal on 8090 serving only POST /usernames/check, admitted by NetworkPolicy to identity-lifecycle alone, so a derivation that 'finds authn's Service' yields a URL that resolves, connects, then 404s or is refused depending on the caller.

service.description: Explicit Service name, REQUIRED when the peer declares no `svcMatch` (e.g. showback). Overrides svcMatch when both are present.

port.description: Explicit port, REQUIRED when the peer declares no `exposePort` (e.g. showback, which is not exposed at all). An exposed peer under exposure.port collapse uses the shared port instead.

mcpBackend.description: #116 roll-guard marker: this component's pod is an MCP backend routed through the agentgateway proxy (kagent for kagent-tools; the repo/config-refs/clickhouse MCP servers; core-provider-agent which bundles the chart-gate MCP). compositions.yaml hashes the <name>:<version> of every mcpBackend component and stamps that hash on BOTH the proxy pod template (agentgateway-policies gateway.mcpBackendHash) and every agent pod (rollGuard env), so a version bump rolls proxy + fleet together and they re-resolve / re-init their pinned MCP sessions.

modelOwner.description: This component OWNS the shared ModelConfigs the rest of the fleet references (model-configs). It is NOT an `agent` (it deploys no Agent), but takes the same .vertexAI injection and agentgateway.enabled, plus the .localModel injection and the agentgateway LLM-route wiring that are its alone. Distinct from `orchestrator` — owning the fleet's models and orchestrating the fleet are different jobs on different components.

namespace.description: Where this component's CompositionDefinition is placed, instead of namespaces.krateo. WHAT ELSE IT MOVES DEPENDS ON THE COMPONENT KIND, and the two cases are different enough to state separately. On an APPENDED registerOnly catalog blueprint (convention krateo-bp-<name>) only the DEFINITION moves: registerOnly emits no Composition, so nothing is left behind in namespaces.krateo and instances are created by their users wherever they choose; `readerGroups` then grants those groups a namespaced Role to see it on the Blueprints page. On a PINNED component it ALSO MOVES THE COMPOSITION INSTANCE, and therefore the helm release the cdc creates -- which is the whole point: a release's identity is name+namespace, and compositions.yaml pins `krateo.io/release-name: <component name>`, so `namespace: X` makes the cdc target release <name> in namespace X. That is what lets the installer ADOPT an existing hand-installed release in place (core-provider applies with TakeOwnership) instead of standing a second copy up beside it. Diego decided 2026-11-16 that the installer adopts demo's hand-installed Kyverno this way, and kyverno is the precedent. THIS WAS FORBIDDEN ON A PINNED COMPONENT UNTIL 2026-11-17 and the guard said so; it was narrowed, not deleted, and this description said the opposite until 2026-11-21. THE HAZARD THE OLD GUARD WAS PROTECTING, which no template can detect and which therefore belongs in the pin's own review: if the component ALREADY has a composition in namespaces.krateo, adding `namespace` is a CROSS-NAMESPACE MIGRATION rather than a rename -- the new instance is created and the old removed inside one upgrade, and the release is renamed with it. Where the component has no composition yet it is a plain create, and adoption of a same-named release already in the target namespace is the intended outcome. So before adding this key to a pinned component, check EVERY cluster that will take the tag for an existing composition and an existing release of that name. The namespace is created if absent and kept on uninstall, because deleting it would take any objects people put there with it; an empty namespace left after an uninstall is expected. Moving an existing definition needs core-provider with the one-controller-per-version hand-over (core-provider#203).

nodePort.description: Pinned NodePort for a browser-facing (expose:true) component when exposure.type=NodePort — deterministic + host-mappable. Wired to spec.service.nodePort in composition mode.

orchestrator.description: This agent is the fleet's ORCHESTRATOR (krateo-autopilot): it auto-attaches every deployed, feature-enabled `agent` component as an A2A sub-agent via extraAgents. Split out of modelOwner, which now marks the ModelConfig owner instead.

pool.description: MEMBERSHIP, NOT SIZING. Threaded onto the component CompositionDefinition's spec.controller.pool. Setting it makes this definition a member of the named cdc pool: core-provider stops running a dedicated <resource>-<version>-controller Deployment for it, and the pool's cdc-pool-<name> Deployment runs it instead. THIS IS A DIFFERENT KNOB FROM core-provider.cdc.pool.{default,overrides}, which SIZES a pool's Deployment (resources and total workers). Sizing is core-provider's values; membership is per-definition and lives here. I carried the two as one thing until core-provider separated them. spec.controller.workers is PER CONTROLLER and keeps its meaning for a pool member; cdc.pool.*.workers is the pool's TOTAL across its members. A pool is created on its FIRST member and later members join it, so adding three definitions to a new pool in one change and adding them one at a time measure different mechanisms. REQUIRES core-provider >= 2.13.113: before that, a CompositionDefinition's Ready and ControllerActive were read from <resource>-<version>-controller for EVERY definition including pool members, and cutover deletes that Deployment -- so a member would have read Ready=False/Creating indefinitely with its composition perfectly healthy (core-provider #581). The reason there is `Creating`, which is already a known reason, so a reason-registry gate stays SILENT and only an age-based check fires, with nothing unusual pointing at the cause.
pool.title: cdc pool membership

readerGroups.description: Groups that may see this blueprint on the Blueprints page: a Role reading compositiondefinitions in the blueprint `namespace`, bound to each group (never a ClusterRole). Requires `namespace` set to a blueprint namespace other than namespaces.krateo.

registerOnly.description: Catalog blueprint: Pass A registers this component's CompositionDefinition (making the blueprint available in the portal) but Pass B never emits a Composition for it — the operator/end-user instantiates it on demand. Use for tenant workload blueprints (e.g. openstack) that ship in the catalog rather than being auto-installed. Typically paired with tier: catalog.

repo.description: OCI registry base overriding ociRepo for this component's chart URL.

requireApproval.description: GRANULAR kagent HITL override (compositions.yaml): the exact list of this agent's tool names that pause for human approval. When present it is threaded onto the agent's spec verbatim and the coarse global .hitlApproval boolean is NOT applied to this agent. Use [] for an agent whose only mutating-shaped tool is a NON-mutating validator (e.g. frontend-agent's k8s_apply_manifest server dry-run) so its authoring loop is not gated — the real write gate stays downstream (publishPage blast-radius). Omit the key entirely for agents that should inherit the coarse global gate on their own mutating tools.

requiresApiGroups.description: HARD render-time requirements, as API GROUPS this component's chart renders objects of (e.g. kagent.dev). Pass B emits the Composition only once every listed group has a served CRD in the cluster. Unlike `deps` -- an ORDERING constraint that inst.depsReady SKIPS when the dep's own feature is disabled -- a missing group suppresses emission for any reason it is missing. Use it whenever the chart renders a kind it does not itself ship: without that kind chart-inspector cannot render the chart at all and the composition 500s every reconcile forever (installer 0.3.474 did exactly this to krateo-demo via builder-gate -> kagent.dev). The unit is a GROUP, not a component: krateo-demo serves six cert-manager.io CRDs from a hand-install while the installer's cert-manager component is absent, so a component-keyed requirement would wrongly suppress two working compositions. Pass A never renders the chart with values and so cannot fail this way, and is not gated.

resources.description: Per-Kind CDC controller compute resources (corev1.ResourceRequirements), threaded onto the component CompositionDefinition's spec.controller.resources. IT REPLACES the core-provider chart's cdc.resources rather than merging with it, so a pin that sets this must set ALL of requests.cpu, requests.memory and limits.memory or it silently drops a default. Set NO cpu limit: a 500m limit throttled the engine in ~99.8% of CFS periods during the cold-start burst, and core-provider's own values.yaml marks the omission deliberate. requests.memory is ALSO GOMEMLIMIT (cdc.goMemLimit: request), so it is at once the eviction floor and the Go heap ceiling -- below a controller's measured peak it GC-thrashes. Absent -> the shared cdc.resources default applies (128Mi request / 512Mi limit) and the CD renders byte-identically. THIS USED TO SAY spec.resources, which the CRD does not declare, so every value set here was pruned by the apiserver while the write reported success.

serviceValuesPath.description: Dotted path to the component chart's Service values block when it is NOT the chart top-level `service` (e.g. kagent's UI Service lives at `kagentapp.ui.service`). The exposure layer builds this nested path and sets `.type` = .Values.exposure.type, flipping the right Service to LoadBalancer/NodePort while the component chart keeps its default.

statusDataTemplate.description: Pass-through to the generated CompositionDefinition's spec.statusDataTemplate — extra fields projected onto the composition's status each reconcile. THE FIELD NAMES ARE forPath AND expression, not path/value: typed from the live core.krateo.io/v1alpha1 CRD, where both are required with minLength 1. The CRD's free-form `schema` field is deliberately NOT exposed, for the same reason as apiRef.extras. Same registerOnly scope, no default, and the same snowplow >= 1.12.38 floor as apiRef.

expression.description: A ${ jq } program over the projection root; a bare path is the trivial copy, and a plain literal with no ${ } wrapper is written verbatim.

forPath.description: Dotted path under .status to write, e.g. "url" or "network.host".

preserveUnknownFields.description: Generate the status node with x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields. Mutually exclusive with type.

type.description: Pins the generated status property's scalar JSON-schema type.

targetRef.description: Deliver this component to a REMOTE cluster: rendered as the CompositionDefinition's spec.deploy.targetRef (installer#579). The composition-dynamic-controller, the generated CRD and the RBAC are created in the named KubernetesTarget's cluster instead of this one. OMIT IT and the CompositionDefinition renders byte-identically to today -- this is inert unless set, like apiRef and statusDataTemplate. THE KubernetesTarget MUST EXIST IN THE SAME NAMESPACE AS THE CompositionDefinition: the CRD gives targetRef only a `name`, resolved in the referencing object's own namespace, so there is no way to point at a target elsewhere. The installer does NOT verify it exists -- that would need `lookup`, which `helm template` disables, so the check would pass vacuously in every render. core-provider fails closed when the target is absent. CREDENTIALS ARE THE OPERATOR'S: the target's kubeconfig or token, and any per-target signing key, are created by the operator and referenced by name. The installer generates neither and no credential passes through a render path.

name.description: Name of the KubernetesTarget, resolved in the CompositionDefinition's own namespace. Mirrors the CRD field exactly; the CRD requires it.

targetRef.title: targetRef

upstream.description: Declares that this component's APPLICATION belongs to another project, not to Krateo. Set it only on a genuinely third-party chart, or on a Krateo chart that wraps a third-party app. It changes one thing: check-pin-ci stops resolving the chart's appVersion to a tag in a source repo, because for someone else's app that resolution either fails outright or aims the gate at an upstream project's CI -- a green tick from a pipeline Krateo does not own, which is a different claim wearing the same colour. Any chartVersion-to-tag route in a Krateo source repo is STILL asserted, so a Krateo chart wrapping a third-party app keeps its own commit verified. The flag is deliberately explicit and never inferred: an inferred exemption is how a Krateo-owned component would drift into 'unverified' with nobody choosing it. check-pins still requires the chart to resolve in the registry.

components.title: Component DAG (advanced override)

core-provider.description: Values passed to the core-provider subchart. Deliberately FREE-FORM apart from the node below: core-provider is a Chart.yaml dependency, so its whole values surface must pass through, and crdgen renders a property-less object as x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields, which is why an Installer CR can carry anything here and nothing prunes it.

resources.title: Resources of the pool's controller container

workers.title: Total concurrent reconciles across the pool's members

resources.title: Resources of the pool's controller container

workers.title: Total concurrent reconciles across the pool's members

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: chart-inspector's pod termination budget in seconds (core-provider#582). Covers the preStop sleep, then the drain of in-flight renders; chart-inspector's own shutdown deadline is this minus preStopSleepSeconds minus 5, and the chart refuses a value that leaves no drain time.

serviceAccount.description: DECLARED ONLY TO WITHHOLD `create`. Everything else under core-provider still passes through untouched; this one node is closed because a chart whose RoleBinding subjects follow a serviceAccountName helper binds the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount when create=false and name is empty -- and in krateo-system 12 pods already run as `default`. The same hazard is closed for oasgen-provider and snowplow in this change. Set `name` to use a pre-created ServiceAccount; the subchart still creates one by default.

create.description: PINNED TO true, not removed. The subchart's own values.yaml sets {create: true, automount: true, annotations: {}, name: ''}, and helm validates this schema against COALESCED values -- coalesceDeps always merges a dependency's defaults in -- so a node omitting `create` can NEVER render. CI refused exactly that. `enum: [true]` instead refuses only the dangerous value: with create=false and an empty name this chart's RoleBinding subjects resolve to the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount, and 12 pods in krateo-system already run as `default`. Plain JSON Schema, so no CEL and no cost budget.
create.title: Create service account (must stay true)

serviceAccount.title: Service account

exposure.description: Exposure model for browser-facing components. LoadBalancer/NodePort set spec.service.type and are resolved via Helm lookup at reconcile time; Gateway keeps Services ClusterIP and emits one Gateway API HTTPRoute per exposed component, attached to a BYO Gateway.

baseDomain.description: Per-component hostnames are derived as <svcMatch>.<baseDomain> (authn.<baseDomain>, snowplow.<baseDomain>, ...). Override any single host via exposure.hosts.<component-name>. Used only when type=Gateway; the frontend config peer URLs become https://<host>.
baseDomain.title: Base domain (type=Gateway)

gatewayMode.description: host (default): each exposed component gets its own hostname + HTTPRoute on the BYO gatewayRef; frontend peer URLs become https://<host>. path: route the whole portal stack (frontend/authn/snowplow/sse-proxy) through the agentgateway on ONE listener at per-component paths (portal at the origin /, /auth -> authn, /content -> snowplow, /events -> sse-proxy; paths/rewrite/auth are component-pins content), flip those Services to ClusterIP, emit the route table as agentgateway-policies spec.platformRoutes, and compute the frontend peer URLs as http://<gateway-ip>:<platformPort><path>. Only used when type=Gateway; INERT unless set to path.
gatewayMode.title: Gateway routing mode (type=Gateway)

gatewayRef.description: The Gateway API Gateway the emitted HTTPRoutes attach to (parentRef). BYO / agentgateway — the installer does NOT create the Gateway or its CRDs. Required when type=Gateway.

namespace.description: Defaults to namespaces.krateo when unset.

gatewayRef.title: Gateway reference (type=Gateway)

hosts.description: Explicit hostname per component name (keys are component names, e.g. frontend), overriding the <svcMatch>.<baseDomain> derivation. Use for the frontend (e.g. portal.<domain> or the apex) or any component that shouldn't follow the derived pattern.
hosts.title: Per-component hostname overrides (type=Gateway)

internalDataPlane.description: When true (path mode only), the primary agentgateway proxy Service (krateo-agent-gateway) is flipped to ClusterIP so the agent data-plane listener (:8080, carrying /llm/v1, /mcp and A2A) has no external path, and a SEPARATE platform Gateway (krateo-agent-gateway-platform) is provisioned as a LoadBalancer carrying ONLY the platform listeners (the portal on :443/:80 and HyperDX on :3000). In-cluster consumers are unaffected (the primary Service name/DNS is unchanged). Closes the open /llm/v1 Vertex proxy at the source. Off/absent => nothing changes.
internalDataPlane.title: Close the agent data plane to the internet (type=Gateway, gatewayMode=path)

platformPort.description: The single listener port the path-mode portal routes are served on (default 80). Only used when type=Gateway AND gatewayMode=path: it is baked into the frontend peer URLs (http://<gateway-ip>:<platformPort><path>) and the platform-http listener the agentgateway-policies chart programs from spec.platformRoutes. Distinct from the gateway's own A2A listener port (8080), which the Autopilot URL keeps.
platformPort.title: Platform listener port (type=Gateway, gatewayMode=path)

port.description: Optional. Overrides the single port browser-facing (expose:true, top-level Service) components are exposed on — sets both their Service port and the frontend config.json peer URLs (http://<lb-ip>:<port>). Unset => each component keeps its per-component exposePort default. Nested-Service (kagent) and own-LB (hyperdx) components are set via componentValues. Ignored when type=Gateway (routing is by hostname).
port.title: Exposure port

tls.description: Serve the whole single-origin portal stack over HTTPS on one hostname. Only used when type=Gateway AND gatewayMode=path AND tls.enabled. The agentgateway terminates TLS on a platform-https:443 listener (certificateRef Secret), the frontend peer URLs become https://<host>/…, and the Autopilot rail's /api/a2a is served over the same :443 listener (JWT edge preserved). Off (default) => everything stays http:// on the platform port, byte-identical.

certificateRef.description: Name of the kubernetes.io/tls Secret (in the gateway/platform namespace) holding the cert+key for host — e.g. one issued by cert-manager. Bound to the platform-https listener's tls.certificateRefs.

enabled.description: Turn on path-mode HTTPS. Default false.

host.description: The single portal hostname (e.g. portal.krateo.dev). All four browser URLs become https://<host>/… and the gateway's platform-https listener terminates TLS for it.

tls.title: Path-mode portal TLS (type=Gateway, gatewayMode=path)

voice.description: One knob for the Autopilot dictation feature. When true it (a) derives the frontend's AUTOPILOT_VOICE_TRANSCRIBE_URL as https://<exposure.tls.host>/stt/v1/chat/completions (no hardcoded per-install host) and (b) turns on the /stt/v1 transcription route (agentgateway-policies stt.enabled) — voice needs both a secure context and that route. REQUIRES exposure.tls (path-mode HTTPS): dictation's getUserMedia needs a secure context, and the render fails loudly if voice is set without it. Off/absent => no voice UI (frontend DOM byte-identical), no /stt/v1 route.
voice.title: Enable Autopilot voice/dictation (requires exposure.tls, path mode)

exposure.title: Exposure

externalDns.description: #115: passthrough to the external-dns blueprint's curated surface, applied when features.externalDns is on. The platform gateway is annotated with exposure.tls.host automatically (compositions.yaml forcePaths gateway.platformHostname), so external-dns keeps the portal's DNS record following the LoadBalancer IP.

domainFilters.description: Zones external-dns may manage, e.g. ["krateo.dev"]. Empty => none; scope it to your zone.

env.description: Provider credentials + tuning as container env, e.g. CF_API_TOKEN via a secretKeyRef (the operator creates the Secret out-of-band).

policy.description: upsert-only (SAFE: create/update, never delete) | sync (also deletes records external-dns owns) | create-only.

name.description: DNS provider (cloudflare, aws, google, azure, ...) — whatever the upstream sigs/external-dns chart supports.

sources.description: Resource kinds external-dns watches for hostnames, e.g. service, gateway-httproute, ingress.

txtOwnerId.description: Ownership id for the TXT registry so external-dns only touches records it created.

externalDns.title: external-dns configuration (features.externalDns)

accessReview.description: Opt-in. Periodic access-review campaigns over the roles Krateo binds (component access-review, with access-review-crd for its AccessReviewCampaign CRD). Defaults false because it is a new component and `features.*` is inert on an upgrade, so enabling it is a deliberate CR edit. The CRD carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so disabling the feature drains the component without deleting any campaign.

agentGateway.description: Opt-in agent gateway: an agentgateway data plane in front of the kagent fleet (components agentgateway-controller + agentgateway-policies, from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-agentiko/charts), giving JWT authentication and per-user RBAC over which agent a caller may reach, which MCP tools it may run and which sub-agents it may delegate to. A valid token becomes mandatory on every agent endpoint, so it never turns on through an upgrade. Needs coreAgents and an issuer whose JWKS the gateway trusts (authn, via portal, by default). Every setting is the policies chart's own: componentValues.agentgateway-policies.

auditWorm.description: Opt-in tamper-EVIDENT mirror of the krateo_audit table (component krateo-audit-worm). The audit table is ordinary ClickHouse, so anyone who can write it can rewrite it; this maintains a separate WORM copy plus a hash-chained seal, and a verifier that reports RED when the chain breaks or the materialized view is dropped. A reset chain stays tampered permanently rather than re-sealing clean. Default false: it needs the krateo_audit table, which only exists once the daemonset collector's clickhouse/audit exporter has created it, and the seal Job fails loudly and retries on its next schedule until then.

capabilityRoles.description: Install krateo-capability-roles: the capability catalog's aggregating ClusterRoles, its Capabilities & roles settings page (Form/Table/Flex/PageHeader + a RESTAction), and optionally the tenant-reader Kyverno policies. OFF by default. ADOPTION TARGET: this chart is already hand-installed on krateo-demo at 0.6.2, so enabling it there is a takeover of an existing release, not a fresh install. REQUIRES KYVERNO ONLY IF componentValues['krateo-capability-roles'].tenantReader.enabled is true (the chart default): templates/tenant-reader-policies.yaml renders ValidatingPolicy and GeneratingPolicy on policies.kyverno.io/v1. Measured: enabled=true renders 14 objects with 6 policies.kyverno.io references, enabled=false renders 11 with none. There is deliberately no requiresApiGroups on the pin, because a hard group requirement would block every cluster that does not need the policies — krateo-057 has 0 kyverno CRDs. Set tenantReader.enabled=false on any cluster without Kyverno; leaving it true there fails loudly at render, which is intended.
capabilityRoles.title: Capability roles

cloudnativePg.description: The CloudNativePG operator for consumers other than Keycloak (kagent's Postgres). cloudnative-pg names `keycloak` as its feature and `cloudnativePg` in alsoFeatures, so either flag turns it on and neither forces the other. Leaving this false while keycloak is true is demo's current state and changes nothing there.

codegenAgents.description: LEGACY — keep false. The codegen/conversion specialists (code-analysis, ansible-to-operator, tf-provider-to-operator, tf-to-helm) were retired in #144, and krateo-blueprint-agent is DRAINING behind this flag on its way out: core-provider-agent is the sole blueprint author. Enabling it redeploys a retired agent that nothing routes to. Default false.

configConnector.description: Opt-in Google Config Connector: the operator and its two CRDs (components gcp-configconnector-crd + gcp-configconnector, from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-blueprints/charts), letting Compositions provision real Google Cloud resources. Runs in CLUSTER mode by default, which means ONE Google service account for the entire cluster and a controller that watches every namespace -- namespaced mode exists but requires Workload Identity and cannot use a key Secret. Needs a Google service-account key in the Secret named by componentValues.gcp-configconnector.configConnector.credentialSecretName, created in cnrm-system after the operator first runs. Applying the ConfigConnector CR makes the operator install ~635 further CRDs, so this measurably grows the cluster's API surface.

coreAgents.description: Deploy the base agent layer: kagent-crds -> kagent -> model-configs (the kagent ModelConfigs the whole fleet references by name) + installer-agent + krateo-autopilot (which also brings up repo-mcp-server, the fleet's grounding server) + incident-agent (alert root-cause analysis) + core-provider-agent, the sole blueprint author (promoted here 2026-09-25 as krateo-blueprint-agent began draining; krateo-autopilot already depended on it). Default false.

coreProvider.description: Engine-present marker (core-provider is always-on via bootstrap). Gates no component.

externalDns.description: #115: opt-in external-dns (DNS record publication) STANDALONE — does NOT require features.ingress, so it works with the agentgateway-controller path. Configure the top-level `externalDns` block (provider + credentials env + domainFilters). Pairs with exposure.tls.host: the platform gateway is annotated with that host so external-dns publishes/updates the portal's DNS record following the LoadBalancer IP (DNS-follows-LB, no static IP, no manual record). Default false.

githubProviderKogConfig.description: Opt-in. Installs the two install-level Configurations that BUILDER PUBLISHING needs (RepositoryConfiguration and PullRequestConfiguration, both named github-blueprints-config) into the release namespace. OFF BY DEFAULT and it must stay off on any cluster where those Configurations were applied by hand -- enabling it there TAKES THEM OVER, which is untested; krateo-057 is exactly that case. Needs github-provider-kog, and that component's `kinds` must include Repository and PullRequest: neither deps nor requiresApiGroups can see that, so a render guard in definitions.yaml refuses the combination.

identityLifecycle.description: Opt-in. Reconciles downstream identity CRs for a user's lifecycle (component identity-lifecycle, with identity-lifecycle-crd for its UserLifecycle CRD). Defaults false because it is a new component and `features.*` is inert on an upgrade, so enabling it is a deliberate CR edit rather than something a version bump can switch on. The CRD carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, so disabling the feature drains the component without deleting any UserLifecycle object.

ingress.description: Opt-in edge layer: gateway-api-crds + agentgateway + cert-manager + cert-manager-issuers (ACME certificate issuance) from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-blueprints/charts. Default false — the base install is unchanged and pulls nothing from krateo-blueprints unless enabled. Turn off if you run behind your own ingress controller / cloud LB / mesh, or manage DNS+certs yourself. Precondition when enabled: cert-manager-issuers' ACME HTTP-01 solver assumes the Gateway API edge is present. NOTE: external-dns moved to its own `externalDns` feature (#115); a host-mode ingress install that also wants DNS enables BOTH ingress and externalDns.

internalTls.description: authn#145: opt-in internal TLS. Enables cert-manager-issuers (the CA ClusterIssuer) and trust-manager (CA distribution as a Bundle). Deliberately SEPARATE from `ingress`, which also brings gateway-api-crds and is therefore mutually exclusive with agentGateway (#557) for reasons unrelated to TLS; before this flag an agentGateway cluster could not obtain a CA issuer at all. cert-manager-issuers is reached through alsoFeatures, so either flag enables it and no existing ingress install is changed. cert-manager is NOT included: issuers and trust-manager declare requiresApiGroups [cert-manager.io] so a hand-installed cert-manager satisfies them and our blueprint is never rendered over it (the cdc sets TakeOwnership unconditionally since core-provider 2.13.82). INCOMPLETE: the Bundle object needs a template in the cert-manager-issuers chart, which lives in krateo-blueprints and is not written yet.

keycloak.description: Opt-in. Installs the Keycloak realm stack that fronts Krateo sign-in. SIX components, all gated on this one flag: keycloak-operator (provides k8s.keycloak.org), cloudnative-pg (provides postgresql.cnpg.io for the embedded database), external-secrets (provides external-secrets.io and generators.external-secrets.io), keycloak itself, keycloak-config-kog (turns realm configuration -- identity provider, authentication flows, required actions, mappers -- into CRs) and krateo-keycloak-realm. OFF by default because it creates a realm and an identity broker, which is a policy decision rather than a default; and `features.*` is inert on an upgrade, so enabling it is a deliberate CR edit. It does NOT create authn's OIDCConfig OBJECT: the CRD (oidcconfigs.oidc.authn.krateo.io) is owned by the authn-crd release, and the realm stack creates the object. HISTORY, kept because the correction matters: this text used to say the flag did NOT install keycloak-config-kog, because the floor was >= 0.5.1 -- that version renders the execution controller's authn ServiceAccount allowlist CR plus its two Roles, and at 0.5.0 authn refuses the execution controller with 403 'not in the exchange allowlist', so the locked first-broker-login flow and the browser-flow redirector never reconcile. The pin has been at or above 0.5.1 since, so the note became false while still being read as current. BEFORE ENABLING ON A GATEWAY/PATH-MODE CLUSTER: exposure.hosts and exposure.baseDomain are HOST-MODE ONLY, so Keycloak cannot be given a subdomain while gatewayMode=path -- it needs a path entry in the generated platformRoutes table AND Keycloak's http-relative-path, so that the issuer its tokens carry is stable. Check also for pre-existing UNOWNED keycloak.ogen.krateo.io CRDs: a CRD with a dangling owner blocks oasgen regeneration, so a RestDefinition can report Ready while the CRD keeps its OLD schema (krateo-057 has six such CRDs from 2026-09-09).

oasgenProvider.description: Deploy oasgen-provider (generates operators from OpenAPI specs).

openstack.description: Install openstack-capabilities: the openstack-view, -provision, -decommission and -compute-tier-guard ClusterRoles plus the compute-tier ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (failurePolicy Fail, one validation, no matchConditions). Per-cluster and only where OpenStack is offered, so OFF by default. Install it BEFORE the first Openstack instance: openstack-provision is what lets a non-admin create one, and the compute-tier guard matches CREATE, so a guard installed by that create's own release never sees the create that matters. On a cluster that previously ran the 0.3.46/0.3.47 openstack umbrella the six objects are owned by that release; the cdc sets TakeOwnership unconditionally (core-provider 2.13.82, composition.go) so adoption needs no knob, and the blueprint stops rendering an object once another release owns it. NO componentValues entry exists by design: the chart's serviceContract default is the canonical contract and a per-instance Composition override is not knowable from here, so overrides are deliberately not expressible (openstack-as-a-service's decision, so their schema stays the single source).
openstack.title: OpenStack capabilities

portal.description: The non-agent platform: authn/snowplow/frontend/portal + portal-starter + the observability stack (operators, krateo-observability, otel collectors, sse-proxy the portal's events bell consumes).

publicPages.title: Public pages
publicPages.description: Opt-in. Installs public-pages: the unauthenticated access-request screens, as CRs only (no workload) in their own namespace krateo-public, served by the existing frontend SPA at /public/<slug>. DEFAULTS FALSE AND MUST: these pages are reachable with no Authorization header, so turning this on is an exposure decision for that cluster, not packaging. It does NOT by itself make them readable -- that needs componentValues.snowplow.publicIdentity.enabled, and the forms need features.identityLifecycle for the intake they post to. Any one of the three missing gives pages that render and do not work.

repoGraph.description: Opt-in the repo-mcp-server DOMAIN-graph / OKF tools (graph_find, graph_map, graph_neighbors, graph_path, knowledge_lookup) — multi-hop structural, reverse-impact and curated-provenance answers grep cannot give. Unlike structureGraph this deploys NO new component: it flips a config layer on three EXISTING coreAgents components in LOCKSTEP — the server (repo-mcp-server graph.enabled) and its consumers' toolNames (krateo-autopilot, incident-agent, via each pin's graphToggle) — so it can never half-enable into the silent Accepted-but-empty server/agent mismatch the repo-mcp-server chart warns about. Distinct from structureGraph (the separate code-STRUCTURE AST server). Needs coreAgents. Default false: more grounding tools is not always better — measure (the repo-mcp-server grounding eval harnesses / a bench A/B) before defaulting on.

selfservice.description: Install selfservice-status: the RESTAction that gives a SelfserviceKrateo composition its portal URL, plan and trial deadline, read from the one HTTPRoute the blueprint labels krateo.io/portal-route. OFF by default because the base installer ships no selfservice blueprint, so without this flag no customer gets its CompositionDefinition or RESTAction. Turning it on is a deliberate CR edit: features.* in a values file is SILENTLY INERT on an upgrade. The RESTAction lands in namespaces.krateo (every component Composition does), so a consuming CompositionDefinition sets apiRef.namespace to that namespace, NOT to the blueprint's own. Requires snowplow and authn, and a snowplow at or above 1.12.38 for the consumer's spec.apiRef to work at all.
selfservice.title: Selfservice status projection

serviceDesk.description: Install the service-desk page: a ticket queue plus a separate raise-a-ticket screen. OFF by default and deliberately NOT folded into `portal` the way the other pages are, because this chart CREATES two namespaces and a Ticket CRD, and its authorization is a policy decision rather than a default: requesterGroups grants create-without-read on the queue, readerGroups grants the desk itself. Enabling it with neither set installs a queue nobody can open and a form nobody can post to.
serviceDesk.title: Service desk

showback.description: Opt-in showback (usage/cost records). Default false because it is only useful once its ClickHouse target exists: the chart's migration creates the `showback` database and its tables on first start, against the clickstack ClickHouse that features.portal brings up via krateo-observability. Enabling it without that ClickHouse leaves the pod retrying its migration. NOTE: features.* is EXCLUDED from the self-bootstrap upgrade patch, so setting this in a values file on an UPGRADE is silently inert — enabling it on a live cluster is an Installer CR edit.

sloRollup.description: Install krateo-slo-rollup: a CronJob that applies a ClickHouse daily rollup table (krateo_slo_daily) and a refreshable view, so a rolling 28-day SLO can be computed although every otel_* table keeps only 7 days. OFF by default. It adds no ingest path and nothing to the insert path of the otel_metrics tables. Requires the observability stack and the collector's source tables: installed before them the Job fails with a clear message, and with the tables present but empty it succeeds with zero rows. Changing rollup.ttlDays on a LIVE cluster later needs an ALTER TTL grant the shipped otelcollector grants do not include -- the Job then fails and logs the exact statement to run.
sloRollup.title: SLO rollup

specialistAgents.description: Deploy the 4 component specialist agents (authn/snowplow/frontend/clickstack) + clickhouse-mcp (needs coreAgents).

structureGraph.description: Deploy structure-graph-mcp-server, the code-STRUCTURE grounding layer (a Graphify tree-sitter AST graph of the engine repos: query_graph/shortest_path/get_neighbors/graph_stats). Both consumers — krateo-autopilot and core-provider-agent — reference it off by default, so turning this on without also setting their mcpServers.structureGraph.enabled deploys a server nothing names. Needs coreAgents. Default false.

tenantOnboarding.description: Opt-in. Installs tenant-onboarding: the v2 Kyverno GeneratingPolicy that provisions a tenant's namespace contents (Role, LimitRange, ResourceQuota) plus the two Kyverno aggregation ClusterRoles. OFF by default, and the chart's OWN `enabled` also defaults false, so the component renders ZERO objects until both are on -- that double gate is deliberate: a key that defaults ON in a pinned chart is briefly LIVE during the roll that introduces it even when the CR carries the key to disable it (measured on krateo-057, 2026-11-13: agentgateway-policies' mcpEntry rendered an internet-facing /mcp route for ~43s across helm revisions 160-161 before the CR's enabled:false arrived in 162). REQUIRES KYVERNO, which is NOT an installer component; there is deliberately no requiresApiGroups on the pin for the same reason as krateo-capability-roles. HAND-OVER ORDER: the chart REFUSES to render while the legacy ClusterPolicy tenant-namespace-on-login still exists (refuseWhileLegacyPolicyExists, default true) -- orphan its generate rules and delete it first, or enabling this fails the render with a named message. That refusal is a feature: it makes the ordering structural instead of procedural.
tenantOnboarding.title: Tenant onboarding

global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.
global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

hitlApproval.description: Human-in-the-loop approval gate applied to every vertexAI agent (autopilot orchestrator + subagents): true pauses each mutating tool call for chat approval; false runs autonomously.
hitlApproval.title: HITL approval

internalTls.description: authn#145: internal TLS wiring. ONE value with TWO consumers, derived by the chart into cert-manager-issuers.internalCA.namespace and trust-manager.app.trust.namespace with forcePath, so they cannot disagree. Those two leaves are deliberately NOT declared under componentValues: they are installer-computed and a per-component override could only make them inconsistent.

certManagerNamespace.description: REQUIRED when features.internalTls is true; the render FAILS if empty. The namespace cert-manager RUNS in -- read --cluster-resource-namespace from its deployment. Required rather than defaulted because the two charts' own defaults disagree ('' = the release namespace vs 'cert-manager'), so unset is a guaranteed mismatch that yields a CA ClusterIssuer which never becomes Ready, silently.

localModel.description: Opt-in (off by default). Run the whole agent fleet on one local Ollama model instead of Gemini/Vertex. The modelOwner component renders every model slot as provider Ollama at host, so every agent referencing a slot follows with no per-agent change. Use a tool-calling-capable model (qwen3.6 recommended).

model.description: Local model id pulled in Ollama; must support tool calling.

localModel.title: Local LLM (Ollama)

registryAuth.description: When enabled, every component CompositionDefinition (and the installer's own) gets spec.chart.credentials so core-provider can pull charts from a private/authenticated OCI registry in-cluster.

imagePullSecretName.description: IMAGE-pull, not just chart-pull. The installer derives a dockerconfigjson Secret from the same registryAuth token(s) and injects it into the components shipping private krateo-agentiko images (autopilot's repo-mcp-server, core-provider-agent's chart-gate-mcp-server, agentgateway-policies' cert-replay hop), so a full-fleet install needs no manual ServiceAccount patch. Works in BOTH global mode (the top-level token) and registries[] mode (the entry matching each component's repo, so the image-pull token is exactly the one that authorizes that registry). Empty auto-derives (Secret name krateo-registry-image-pull); set to the name of a pre-existing dockerconfigjson Secret in namespaces.krateo to supply your own.

insecureSkipVerifyTLS.description: Skip TLS verification on the in-cluster chart pull (maps to CompositionDefinition spec.chart.insecureSkipVerifyTLS). Applies to every component (a coarse dev toggle), independent of auth; a registries[] entry may raise it for its own registry.

passwordRef.description: Reference to a Secret holding the registry password/token.

registries.description: Registry-keyed credentials for multi-registry installs. When NON-EMPTY, each component's chart-pull credentials are selected by matching its effective registry base (its `repo` override, else `ociRepo`) against these entries: a matched component gets that entry's credentials; a component whose registry has no entry gets NO credentials, so a token is never presented to a registry it does not belong to. In this mode the global username/passwordRef above are ignored. When EMPTY (default), the legacy global credentials apply to every component unchanged.

insecureSkipVerifyTLS.description: Skip TLS verification for pulls from this registry (overrides the global toggle upward for this repo only).

passwordRef.description: Reference to a Secret holding this registry's password/token.

repo.description: The OCI registry base this credential authenticates, matched verbatim against a component's effective repo (its `repo` override, else `ociRepo`). e.g. oci://ghcr.io/krateo-agentiko/charts

registryAuth.title: Private registry credentials

vertexAI.description: Vertex AI for the autopilot agents via Application Default Credentials (no API key). Requires the GKE node SA to have aiplatform access and the cloud-platform OAuth scope.

secretKey.description: File name inside secretName; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/var/secrets/gcp/<secretKey>. Default key.json.
secretKey.title: Key file inside the Secret

secretName.description: k8s Secret with the GCP service-account key JSON for portable explicit-key ADC (any cluster). Unset => metadata-server ADC (GKE node SA).
secretName.title: Vertex SA-key Secret name

vertexAI.title: Gemini Vertex AI

title: Krateo PlatformOps Installer
